commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix eagle draft sharing with a quantized lm_head
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`_should_share()` in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py` reads `draft.weight` unconditionally to decide whether the draft can adopt the target's `lm_head`:

```python
w = draft.weight
if w.is_cuda and torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(w.device)[0] < w.numel() * 2:
    return torch.equal(w.cpu(), target.weight.cpu())
return torch.equal(w, target.weight)
```

A quantized `ParallelLMHead` registers packed weights (`weight_packed`, `qweight`, ...) and no `weight`, so this raises and aborts engine startup:

```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/eagle/utils.py", line 22, in _should_share
  w = draft.weight
AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

This is a guard that already exists in V1 and was lost in the V2 rewrite. `LLMBaseProposer._maybe_share_lm_head` gates the same comparison on the attribute being present:

```python
elif (
    hasattr(target_language_model, "lm_head")
    and hasattr(target_language_model.lm_head, "weight")
    and hasattr(self.model.lm_head, "weight")
    and isinstance(target_language_model.lm_head.weight, torch.Tensor)
    and isinstance(self.model.lm_head.weight, torch.Tensor)
    and torch.equal(...)
):
    share_lm_head = True
else:
    # "Detected EAGLE model with distinct lm_head weights.
    #  Keeping separate lm_head weights from the target model."
```

When the attribute is missing, V1 falls through to the `else` and keeps the draft's own head. This PR restores that behaviour in the V2 helper.

## Why the draft keeps its own head

Not sharing is the correct answer, not merely the safe one. Without a plain `weight` on both sides there is no way to prove the two copies match, and adopting the target's head would silently change the draft's output.

For eagle3 drafts with a reduced `draft_vocab_size` the decision is unchanged: the shapes differ, so `torch.equal` already returned `False`. Those models get the same answer they did before — without raising.

The helper is shared, so this also covers the dflash and dspark drafters.

## Scope — please read

I could not find a public checkpoint that reproduces this. I scanned 880 eagle3/speculator repos and 429 quantized-target candidates on the Hub, reading safetensors tensor names; none carries a quantized `lm_head` or `embed_tokens`. The closest public eagle3 drafts (`nm-testing/Speculator-*-Eagle3-converted-*-quantized-w4a16`) quantize the transformer layers and leave `lm_head.weight` in place.

So this is a supported-but-uncommon configuration. Quantizing the `lm_head` is first-class in vLLM — `ParallelLMHead` takes a `quant_config`, and `CompressedTensorsConfig.get_quant_method` has a dedicated `isinstance(layer, ParallelLMHead)` branch — it is just rarely shipped. We hit it with internal compressed-tensors checkpoints that quantize the head (`lm_head.weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`, no `lm_head.weight`), which made some of our models fail.

I am raising it because the V1/V2 divergence is a real inconsistency regardless of how many checkpoints exercise it today, not because of the number of users affected. Happy to publish a small reproducer checkpoint to the Hub if a maintainer wants one.

## Not a duplicate

Could not find any.

## Test plan

```
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_spec_decode_eagle_utils.py    # 5 passed
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py  # 2 passed
```

Reverting the fix fails the two quantized-head cases with the exact `AttributeError` above; the three unquantized cases pass either way, confirming the sharing policy is unchanged.

End-to-end on gfx1151 with an internal `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct-AWQ` target and an eagle3 draft whose `lm_head` is int8 compressed-tensors.

`pre-commit` (ruff, mypy) clean.

AI assistance was used for this change.


---

- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: widen skinny GEMM LDS activation loads to b128
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

The `wvSplitK` int4 skinny GEMM stages activations into LDS as `s[k_ + K * n]` and reads them back per row. `K` is a runtime value, so the compiler cannot prove the per-row offset `K*n` is 16-element aligned and falls back to paired `ds_load_2addr_b32`/`b64` for the higher rows. But `K` is a multiple of `A_CHUNK` and so is `k_`, so `s[k_ + K * n]` is in fact `sizeof(bigTypeA)`-aligned for every row — annotating the read lets the compiler widen all activation rows to `ds_load_b128`.

That invariant was implicit: `A_CHUNK` is a template argument pinned to 16 by the launch macro, and the host only checks `K % 16 == 0`. The k-loop already relies on it too, since it consumes whole `A_CHUNK` chunks. The host check now uses a shared `kInt4KAlign` constant, each kernel does `static_assert(kInt4KAlign % A_CHUNK == 0)`, and the LDS buffer is declared `alignas(sizeof(bigTypeA))`, so raising `A_CHUNK` fails to build until `kInt4KAlign` is raised with it.

This is a compiler-visibility argument rather than an architectural one, so it is not gated on a specific gfx target. The global fallback read in the medium kernel is deliberately left untouched: `A[]`'s base alignment is not guaranteed there.

LDS load instructions across all int4 instantiations, gfx1151 with ROCm 10.2, counted by disassembling the gfx1151 device image out of the built `_rocm_C.abi3.so`:

| | `ds_load_b128` | `ds_load_2addr_b32` | `ds_load_2addr_b64` | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 6864 | 3744 | 624 | 11232 |
| after | 9360 | 0 | 0 | 9360 |

`N=1` and `N=2` were already fully widened by this compiler and come out byte-identical; the change is confined to `N=3,4,5`.

## Measurements

`benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_gemm.py`, `--group-size 128`, batch 4, median of 3 passes, TFLOP/s, symmetric / asymmetric:

| K x N | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2048x2048 | 2.501 / 2.020 | 2.929 / 2.316 | **+17.1% / +14.6%** |
| 2560x2560 | 3.040 / 2.853 | 3.392 / 3.038 | **+11.6% / +6.5%** |
| 8192x2048 | 2.218 / 1.645 | 2.276 / 1.743 | +2.6% / +6.0% |
| 2560x3840 | 3.834 / 3.402 | 3.877 / 3.510 | +1.1% / +3.2% |
| 2048x6144 | 3.301 / 3.122 | 3.275 / 3.077 | -0.8% / -1.4% |
| 2048x16384 | 3.258 / 3.162 | 3.272 / 3.164 | +0.4% / +0.1% |
| 2560x19456 | 3.361 / 3.334 | 3.369 / 3.321 | +0.2% / -0.4% |

The win concentrates on small `out_features`, where the kernel is bound by the LDS read rather than by the weight stream. Batch 1 and 2 are flat everywhere, which is exactly what the instruction counts predict. Only shapes that actually reach the HIP skinny path (`M <= 5` and `K*M <= 32768`) are listed; the rest route to Triton and are unaffected.

Reproducing the asymmetric column needs #57004, without which the benchmark's `hybrid-w4a16-zp` provider raises.

## Model evaluation

GSM8K on gfx1151, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42. `max_num_seqs=4` so every decode step runs the `N=3,4` instantiations this change touches (`max_num_seqs=1` would only exercise the unchanged `N=1` path):

```bash
lm_eval --model vllm \
  --model_args pretrained=<model>,max_model_len=4096,max_num_seqs=4,dtype=float16,gpu_memory_utilization=0.75,enforce_eager=False,seed=42 \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size auto --seed 42
```

| model | filter | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` | strict-match | 0.8582 ± 0.0096 | 0.8590 ± 0.0096 |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` | flexible-extract | 0.8613 ± 0.0095 | 0.8620 ± 0.0095 |

Qwen3-8B-AWQ differs by a single question, well inside one stderr. Average output throughput over the eval run is flat (20.9 vs 20.6 tok/s).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` on gfx1151: 84 passed.
- [x] `pre-commit run --files csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` passes, clang-format included.
- [x] ISA verified by disassembling the built device image and counting LDS opcodes per instantiation; the `static_assert`/`alignas` hardening leaves it byte-identical.
- [x] With the launch macro set to `A_CHUNK=32`, the build fails on the `static_assert` in both kernels, and succeeds again once `kInt4KAlign` is raised to 32.
- [x] GSM8K 5-shot on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`: accuracy matches the baseline (see above).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change, as required by `AGENTS.md`. Not a duplicate: the only other open PR touching `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` is #56301, which changes host-side weight row-stride padding and does not touch the LDS activation reads.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Forward launch grid to Triton kernel overrides
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The kernel dispatcher's KernelOverride dropped the caller's launch grid, so platforms could not remap grids (e.g. to physical core counts). Triton kernel implementations are now swapped in directly, launching natively and staying inlinable as Triton device functions; non-Triton implementations are wrapped, receive the grid via __getitem__, and delegate compile-only warmup.

This PR fixes three gaps in the Triton kernel dispatcher: (1) the launch grid is now forwarded to overrides instead of being dropped, (2) Triton device functions called from inside other kernels can be overridden without breaking the outer kernel's compilation, and (3) JIT warmup is delegated to the override instead of failing.

commits.pr_title: [CI][CPU] Initialize DFlash test FC after loading weights
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Closes #63972. Initialize the DFlash dtype regression's FC through its existing post-load hook before the first forward, fixing the deterministic `cpu_linear` error in **CPU-Spec Decode Tests**.

## Claims

- The existing FP32-to-draft-dtype test now runs on a CPU platform.
- Retains the test's dtype and output assertions; no runtime code, skips or tolerances change.

## Validation

macOS arm64, Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0; base `5d35ce39`.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/spec_decode \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py::test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype -q
```

Before: **1 failed** with `AttributeError: 'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'cpu_linear'`. After: **1 passed**.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/spec_decode \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py
git diff --check
```

**26 passed, 92 skipped** (existing accelerator-only cases); applicable hooks and diff check passed. Intel CPU packed-GEMM execution remains pending CI. This test-only setup correction does not change model behavior or require model evaluation.

## Details

The test added in #63436 directly initializes `fc.weight` and calls forward, bypassing the loader's post-load processing. The CPU linear implementation requires that processing to initialize `cpu_linear`. Run the same hook after filling the weight.

The exact base fails in [main CI #97527](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97527#01a17bf7-46e5-4f1f-bc9e-95f8e3cd8d54); #63972 records the traceback and another occurrence. The existing `cpu-spec-decode-tests` job already selects this file, so no CI configuration change is needed.

Duplicate checks found no fix for this test. #55318 concerns Tensorizer loading, and #57733 concerns model-loader finalization; neither covers this direct-construction test. #62796 only records the unrelated CI failure.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, the one-line change, review and local validation.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Drop BasevLLMParameter's Python `__torch_function__`
commits.pr_body: ## Overview `BasevLLMParameter` overrides `__torch_function__` with a Python classmethod. The override only forwards to `Parameter`'s disabled implementation. Since #62326, quantized weights and scales stay `BasevLLMParameter` subclasses after `process_weights_after_loading`. As a result, every eager op that takes one of them goes through Python `handle_torch_function`. This PR removes the override. The subclasses then inherit `torch._C._disabled_torch_function_impl` from `Parameter`, which torch short-circuits in C++. ## Claims - Fixes a host-side regression from #62326 on steps that run outside full CUDA graphs: prefill and mixed prefill+decode steps. - GLM-5.2-FP8, TP4 on one GB300 node, same-node A/B against main on 3 nodes: - c1 TTFT for 1024-token prompts drops from 220.4 to 207.0 ms (-6.1%); - worker `execute_model` host time drops 8.7 ms per prefill step (-4.5%) and 11.2 ms per mixed step (-4.4%); - TPOT is unchanged: pure decode replays full CUDA graphs and dispatches no ops. - No behavior change: - #62326's guarantees are untouched: the same parameter objects, classes, loader attributes and `data_ptr`; - op results were plain tensors before (`super().__torch_function__` is the disabled implementation) and still are; - greedy outputs are identical and GSM8K is within run-to-run noise. ## Validation ### Serving: GLM-5.2-FP8 (`zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8`) Setup: - TP4, one GB300 node, MRV2, default torch.compile and CUDA graphs; - `--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=mnnvl`; - `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching`; - `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos`. At c8/c32, new prompts arrive while others decode, so those runs mix prefill and decode steps. Method: - Each Slurm job runs on one node. It first starts a throwaway server: the first server on a node is 10-15 ms slower at c1 TTFT, so it is excluded. - It then interleaves `main`, `this PR` and two other variants not covered here, twice each. - Values are the mean of each variant's 2 runs on that node; the delta is against `main` on the same node. Median TTFT (ms): | node / job | workload | main | this PR | delta | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | c1, 24 prompts | 223.5 | **204.7** | **-18.7** | | 2 | c1 | 220.5 | **210.5** | **-10.1** | | 3 | c1 | 217.3 | **205.7** | **-11.6** | | **mean** | **c1** | **220.4** | **207.0** | **-13.5 (-6.1%)** | | mean | c8, 160 prompts | 465.7 | **453.1** | **-12.6** | | mean | c32, 320 prompts | 810.2 | **762.1** | **-48 (noisy)** | Median TPOT (ms): c1 9.70 vs 9.69, c8 14.30 vs 14.27, c32 25.80 vs 25.77. Host time of the worker's `GPUModelRunner.execute_model`: a `perf_counter` wrapper, with steps split by kind. Values are the p50 per rank, averaged over the 4 ranks, from the same runs (c1 + c8 workloads): | node / job | prefill-only step: main | this PR | delta | mixed step: main | this PR | delta | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 189.8 | **181.0** | **-8.8** | 254.5 | **239.3** | **-15.2** | | 2 | 192.5 | **184.2** | **-8.3** | 257.4 | **248.6** | **-8.8** | | 3 | 191.7 | **182.8** | **-8.9** | 254.0 | **244.5** | **-9.6** | An earlier stack-sampling profile of the prefill step put about 14% of its host time in `parameter.py:__torch_function__`. It was called from the FP8 linear apply, the DeepGEMM / per-token-group quant wrappers and the FlashInfer TRT-LLM FP8 MoE calls. Dense BF16 model (Qwen3-0.6B, TP1): no measurable change (c1 TTFT 22.4 vs 22.3/23.3 ms, c32 within noise). Its unquantized weights were already `ModelWeightParameter` before #62326, and its steps are less host-bound. ### Correctness - Greedy, `temperature=0`, 34 fixed prompts with 128 tokens each at c1: outputs are byte-identical to `main` in 3/3 runs on 3 nodes. - GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, completions, max concurrency 64): | | runs | accuracy | |---|---|---| | main | 5 | 95.0, 94.2, 94.2, 94.9, 94.8 | | this PR | 3 | 94.5, 94.1, 94.2 | The kernels and their inputs are unchanged, so the spread is batch-composition noise at concurrency 64. Main alone spans 94.2 to 95.0. - The serving runs use torch.compile (Dynamo traces modules with these parameters) and CUDA graphs. They start and produce identical outputs without the override. ### Tests ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_utils.py \ tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py \ tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py -k "not test_reload_weights" .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py \ -k "test_reload_weights and (FP8_BLOCK or FP8_DYNAMIC)" pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/parameter.py tests/model_executor/test_utils.py ``` Results on GB300 (this PR vs `main`, same commands): | test | this PR | main | |---|---|---| | `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py` | 14 passed (incl. the new test) | 13 passed | | `tests/quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` | 10 passed | 10 passed | | `test_reload.py -k "not test_reload_weights"` | 70 passed, 2 xpassed, 2 failed | same 2 failures | | `test_reload_weights` FP8_BLOCK / FP8_DYNAMIC (TP1, TP2) | 4 passed, 4 skipped | 4 passed, 4 skipped | | `pre-commit` | all hooks pass | | Both `test_reload.py` failures also fail on `main` and are unrelated: - `test_kv_scale_reload`: perplexity 6575.09 after reload, identical on `main`. - `test_online_quantize_reload[...Qwen3-0.6B...fp8_per_tensor-1]`: when it runs after that failure in the same session, the forked engine core hits `CUDA error: initialization error`. This also happens on `main`. The test passes when run alone on both trees. New test `test_kept_param_ops_skip_python_torch_function`: - it checks that a param kept by `replace_parameter` keeps its class; - that `torch.overrides.has_torch_function` is false for it, so eager ops dispatch in C++; - and that op results are still plain tensors. ## Details **Root cause.** - #23036 added the override, together with a torch-2.7-only `traceable_tensor_subclasses` Dynamo workaround (`_torch27_patch_tensor_subclasses`). - #33209 removed the workaround when torch < 2.8 support was dropped, but left the override. - The override does nothing at runtime: it calls `super().__torch_function__`, i.e. `Parameter`'s `_disabled_torch_function_impl`. Its presence still makes torch treat these parameters as having a Python torch function. Every op, and every Python-level `Tensor` method or property access on them, then goes through `handle_torch_function` and the classmethod. - Before #62326, most quantization methods re-registered plain `Parameter`s in `process_weights_after_loading`, so FP8/FP4 weights and scales did not pay this cost. - #62326 keeps the original objects so that reload and RL refit keep their loader metadata. The quantized weights and scales of every linear and MoE layer now pay this cost on every eager op. **Fix.** Delete the override. `BasevLLMParameter` then behaves like `torch.nn.Parameter`: - `__torch_function__` is the disabled implementation; - `isinstance`, class, attributes and object identity are unchanged; - op results stay plain tensors. This keeps everything #62326 relies on. A global monkey-patch or unwrapping params after loading would undo #62326's goal. **Scope.** - Only steps that dispatch ops eagerly benefit: prefill, mixed and piecewise steps. Full-CUDA-graph decode is unchanged. - The gain grows with the number of quantized layers and ops per step. ## Why this is not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open` searches found no PR that touches `BasevLLMParameter.__torch_function__` or the overhead from #62326. Search terms: `__torch_function__`, `BasevLLMParameter`, `replace_parameter`, `62326`, `torch_function overhead`, `handle_torch_function`, `ModelWeightParameter overhead`. - #62407 (part 3 of the #62326 series, open) changes which params stay registered and does not touch `parameter.py`. This PR is independent of it and helps it as well. - The only earlier change to the override is #25613, reverted by #25681. It returned `NotImplemented` on torch < 2.8 for a Dynamo bug and did not remove the dispatch. - No upstream issue covers it. ## AI assistance AI assistance was used to investigate the regression, write the change and its test, and run the benchmarks and evals above. The submitter reviewed every changed line and the measurements. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Add --reasoning-effort-map to rewrite request reasoning efforts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Rust frontend version of #61094: adds `--reasoning-effort-map`, which rewrites the reasoning effort a client sends into one the chat template supports.

## Claims

- `--reasoning-effort-map '{"medium": "high"}'` rewrites listed efforts; unlisted efforts pass through.
- Works for `vllm-rs serve`, the render server, and the Python-launched frontend (`--args-json`), so it follows #61094's flag once that merges.
- `reasoning_effort` in `chat_template_kwargs` is not rewritten (same as #61094).
- Unknown keys fail at startup.
- With the flag unset, behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

End to end with the render server on `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` (V4.1 rejects `medium`):

| Flag | `reasoning_effort: "medium"` |
|---|---|
| none | 400: `DeepSeek V4.1 reasoning_effort must be low, high, xhigh, max, ...` |
| `{"medium":"high"}` | renders the same tokens as `high` |
| `{"mediun":"high"}` | startup error: ``unknown variant `mediun`, expected one of `none`, ...`` |

Tests:

```bash
cd rust
cargo test -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd     # 468 + 82 passed
cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib             # 358 passed
cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

New tests: the map rewrites the typed effort but not `chat_template_kwargs`, args-json passes the map through, and an unknown key is rejected. `roundtrip_{qwen3,kimi_k25,mimo_v26}` grammar-replay tests fail locally, and they fail the same way on clean `main`.

## Details

The map is applied in `ChatRequestProcessor` before rendering and before the output processor is built, so chat completions, render and tokenize all use it. CLI keys are parsed as `ReasoningEffort`, which is how unknown efforts get rejected. `Config` and `RenderConfig` keep the keys typed and lower them to strings when building the chat processor.

Not a duplicate: no other open PR adds an effort map to the Rust frontend. AI assistance (Claude) was used.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Add per-request speculative decoding metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Adds speculative-decoding acceptance statistics to per-request metrics in the Rust OpenAI frontend.

This is a follow-up to #59314, which added the base per-request timing metrics support. It is not duplicate work: the Rust Chat Completions and Completions routes do not currently propagate the engine's per-request speculative-decoding statistics. This PR reuses the converter already used by `/inference/v1/generate`.

- exposes `metrics.speculative_decoding` for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`
- supports both non-streaming and streaming responses
- emits streaming metrics only on the final usage chunk
- keeps timing metrics and speculative-decoding metrics independently configurable
- reuses the existing speculative-decoding conversion shared with `/inference/v1/generate`

The response follows the existing Python/OpenAI per-request metrics schema, including summary and detailed speculative-decoding modes.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo check --workspace --tests`
- `cargo clippy -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p vllm-server routes::openai::` — 153 passed
- `cargo test -p vllm-text --lib` — 111 passed, 1 ignored
- `cargo test -p vllm-chat --lib` — 389 passed
- focused shared converter and propagation tests
- pre-commit hooks
- A100 end-to-end validation with n-gram speculative decoding:
  - Chat Completions, streaming and non-streaming
  - Completions, streaming and non-streaming
  - timing-only, speculative-decoding-only, and combined response behavior
  - intermediate streaming chunks omit metrics; the final usage chunk includes them

## Notes

A broader `cargo test -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat` run also exercised the integration suites. Two model round-trip snapshot cases (`roundtrip_mimo_v26` and `roundtrip_step5`) failed because the locally resolved model/tokenizer data no longer matched the checked-in snapshots; this PR only adds `spec_decode_metrics: None` to their terminal-output test fixture.

AI assistance was used to implement and validate this change. I reviewed every changed line and understand the implementation.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Group prompt-cache usage and report created_cache_tokens
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR is taken over and reworked from zylen-det's original change, whose description is kept at the end. The original reported `created_cache_tokens` on chat only, through a separate chat constructor. This version restructures the usage types first and keeps the original's CLI help fix. It supersedes vllm-project/vllm#63953.

The Python frontend reports `usage.prompt_tokens_details.created_cache_tokens` (the prompt tokens newly written to the prefix cache, vllm-project/vllm#48535); the Rust frontend does not. Adding it to the current Rust usage path means editing every route and dozens of test literals. Each prefill-stats count travels as a loose scalar through four separate accumulators. The wire usage block also has two constructors, and a route-specific field would have to be patched in at each call site. This PR first groups the counts and gives the wire usage block one constructor, then adds the field on top.

## Claims

- With `--enable-prompt-tokens-details`, the Rust frontend reports `created_cache_tokens` next to `cached_tokens` in non-streaming responses and in streaming usage chunks.
- The first commit is a pure refactor. Afterwards, adding a prefill-stats count touches only `PromptCacheUsage` (`vllm-llm`) and `Usage::from_token_usage` (`vllm-server`). The second commit shows this: 2 production files. The third commit, from the original PR, corrects the `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` help text.

## Validation

Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check   # ok
cargo sort --workspace --check rust                          # ok
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans   # ok
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings   # ok
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
# 2346 tests run: 2346 passed, 13 skipped
```

- `routes::tests::prompt_tokens_details_report_created_cache_tokens` sends chat and completions requests through the HTTP router against a mock engine. The engine sends its prefill stats on the first output only. The test asserts `{"cached_tokens": 2, "created_cache_tokens": 3}` after the later decode output.
- `collect_output_aggregates_raw_tokens_logprobs_and_terminal_metadata` (`vllm-llm`) now also checks the count on the collected output.
- Both tests fail when `PromptCacheUsage::merge` drops the new count.
- The original PR's real-engine comparison (below) covers chat on its implementation; this rework was not rerun against a real engine. The value is the engine's `PrefillStats.num_cache_creation_tokens`, which Python's output processor reads too.

## Details

**Refactor (no behavior change):**
- `PromptCacheUsage` groups the counts that come from the engine's prefill stats. It replaces the loose `cached_token_count` on `GenerateOutput` and `TokenUsage`.
- Prefill stats arrive on one output only, so `PromptCacheUsage::merge` keeps the largest value seen. All four accumulators call it:
  - `GenerateOutput::merge` (stream interval);
  - `collect_output`;
  - the text decode stream;
  - the `/generate` stream.
- `Usage::from_counts` is removed. `Usage::from_token_usage` is the only constructor of the wire usage block. The streaming running-usage snapshot (`ContinuousUsage`) goes through it too, still without prompt details. It destructures its input exhaustively, so a new usage field fails to compile until it is mapped there.

**New field:** `PromptCacheUsage::cache_creation_token_count` → `PromptTokenUsageInfo::created_cache_tokens`.
- As in Python, a remote prefill's `remote_prefill_cached_tokens` overrides only `cached_tokens`.
- gRPC `FinishInfo` is unchanged.

**Divergence:** Python reports `created_cache_tokens` on chat only, where it feeds the Anthropic Messages `cache_creation_input_tokens`. On completions, Python leaves it `null` in non-streaming responses and omits it from streaming usage chunks. Rust reports it wherever `prompt_tokens_details` is reported. This is a strict superset of Python's output. Keeping the chat-only asymmetry would need a per-route switch at the call sites.

## Original description

<details>
<summary>Original description by zylen-det</summary>

### Overview

Report the engine-provided cache-creation count as `usage.prompt_tokens_details.created_cache_tokens` in Rust Chat Completions, matching the Python frontend. Addresses the cache-creation item in #44280.

### Claims

- Reports the count, including zero, in non-streaming responses and final streaming usage chunks when `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` is enabled.
- Preserves prefill counts across subsequent decode outputs without changing token totals.

### Validation

- Route regression covers streaming/non-streaming, details enabled/disabled, and absent/zero/nonzero prefill stats. The new test fails on the base commit and passes with this change.
- **24 real-engine HTTP requests passed** on RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB with Qwen3-0.6B, comparing Python and Rust across both response modes, cold/repeated prompts, and caching/details enabled or disabled.

| Case | cached_tokens (Python / Rust) | created_cache_tokens (Python / Rust) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold prompt | 0 / 0 | 288 / 288 |
| Repeated prompt | 288 / 288 | 0 / 0 |
| Prefix caching disabled | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

With details disabled, neither frontend reports cache counts. Token totals and generated text matched; the comparison does not assert full response-JSON parity.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands and configuration</summary>

Regression test (also run against the base with only the test copied over):

```bash
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --locked -p vllm-server --lib \
  -E 'test(chat_reports_engine_cache_creation_tokens)'
```

Server configuration used for the comparison:

```bash
cargo build --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-cmd --bin vllm-rs --locked

# Python frontend: VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0
# Rust frontend: VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
#   VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH="$PWD/rust/target/debug/vllm-rs"
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --dtype float16 \
  --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.4 --enforce-eager \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --generation-config vllm \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-prompt-tokens-details
```

For the other configurations, omit `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` or replace `--enable-prefix-caching` with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.


GPU validation used FP16, TP=1, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu132, CUDA 13.2, and model revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. Requests used temperature=0, seed=0, max_tokens=16, enable_thinking=false, and separate cache salts for each response mode. Each request had 289 prompt tokens and 16 completion tokens.

</details>

### Details

The engine already supplies `PrefillStats.num_cache_creation_tokens`; the Rust frontend discarded it. This change retains it in the output stream, propagates it through `TokenUsage`, and includes it in chat usage. API documentation and CLI help are updated.

Duplicate-work checks found no overlapping implementation: #60624 covers multimodal counts, #63061 leaves cache-creation reporting to a separate change, and #58885 covers P/D cache-hit reporting.

AI assistance was used. I reviewed every changed line and ran the relevant tests.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Rust Frontend] Skip detokenization for gRPC requests that read no text
[Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 when local media access is disabled
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Return HTTP 400 instead of 500 when a request uses a `file://` media URL on a server started without `--allowed-local-media-path`. Fixes #61874.

## Claims

- Disabled local media access is reported as `400 BadRequestError` on the OpenAI chat and render endpoints (sync and async media loading). It was `500 InternalServerError`.
- The access restriction and the error message are unchanged; no file is read.

## Validation

Before/after on a CPU build (macOS arm64), `HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct`, server started **without** `--allowed-local-media-path`:

```bash
vllm serve HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct --max-model-len 2048 --enforce-eager \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt.image 1 --port 8811
curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n' localhost:8811/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "HuggingFaceTB/SmolVLM-256M-Instruct", "max_tokens": 8,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "Describe this image."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "file:///tmp/vllm-disallowed-image.png"}}]}]}'
```

| | Response |
|---|---|
| main | `{"error":{"message":"Cannot load local files without \`--allowed-local-media-path\`.","type":"InternalServerError","param":null,"code":500}}` HTTP 500 |
| this PR | `{"error":{"message":"Cannot load local files without \`--allowed-local-media-path\`.","type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}}` HTTP 400 |

Terminal captures of the same request (top: `main` @ 9e0bc7a651, bottom: this PR @ bc9eb76e9b):

**Before (main): HTTP 500 `InternalServerError`**

![Before: HTTP 500 InternalServerError](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/pr64032-before.png)

**After (this PR): HTTP 400 `BadRequestError`**

![After: HTTP 400 BadRequestError](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hemuku90/vllm/pr-assets/pr64032-after.png)

Same server with `--enable-scale-out`, `POST /v1/chat/completions/render` with this PR: HTTP 400 `BadRequestError` (the path the new regression test uses).

Unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py -k "test_fetch_image_local_files and not relative and not space"
# main (with updated assertions): 4 failed — RuntimeError: Cannot load local files without `--allowed-local-media-path`.
# this PR:                        4 passed
pytest tests/multimodal/media/test_connector.py tests/multimodal/media/test_unprocessable_entity_error.py
# this PR: 94 passed
```

`tests/entrypoints/scale_out/render/test_render_multimodal.py::test_chat_completion_render_rejects_local_file_when_disabled` reuses the existing `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct` `vision_server` fixture (no extra server start) and runs in the existing `entrypoints/scale_out` Buildkite step. It was not run locally (needs a GPU for that model); the same endpoint and assertion were checked by hand with SmolVLM above.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.

## Details

Root cause: `MediaConnector._load_file_url` raised a bare `RuntimeError` when `allowed_local_media_path` is unset. `create_error_response` maps unclassified exceptions to 500, while the adjacent out-of-directory check raises `ValueError` (400). The fix raises `VLLMValidationError`, the `VLLMClientError` subclass already used in this module, so the status comes from the typed exception path rather than the raw-`ValueError` fallback slated for removal.

Not a duplicate: #61751 handles missing files when local access is *enabled* and does not touch this branch. #63749 is the Rust frontend, which does not support `--allowed-local-media-path`. @ntu-b12505041 expressed interest in #61874 on 2026-10-15 but no PR has been opened since; happy to close this in favor of theirs if one is in progress.

No other code catches `RuntimeError` for this path (only torchcodec decode handlers in `audio.py`, unrelated). The Rust frontend does not support `--allowed-local-media-path`, so no parity change.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Spec Decode] Refactor #41834 with useful improvements
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#41834 has been stale for a while, and many key contributions have been superseded by other PRs. This PR extracts the useful parts of that huge PR and conducts end-to-end experiments on two Sparks to ensure it works well. The authorship is also acknowledged.

## Claims

In general, this PR comprises:

- **mHC residual reuse.** For a `8192` token prefill setup, this saves 256 MiB VRAM.
- **No `_mtp_hidden_buffer` under DSpark.** DSpark does not need and access these memories and this saves another 256 MiB VRAM per card.
- **Stale MRV1 drafter layout caches.** This is a real bugfix but only for V1 runner. This fixes the drafter layout cache and increases the accept rate from 51% to 63%, same as V2 runner.

## Validation

Reproduced on two Sparks. I did several end-to-end experiments using DeepSeek-v4-Flash and ensured that the tokens output is the same.

No performance regression is observed, and I confirm the VRAM savings and draft acceptance rate benefits.

## Details

See above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model] Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: load checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 QSA indexer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #62308. Since #59533, `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` lists `indexer.index_qk_proj`. Quant configs read that class-level mapping before the model is built, so they check q/k/v and the QSA indexer as one fused layer. Checkpoints that quantize q/k/v but keep the indexer in BF16 fail to load with `Found different quantization schemes for the shards of ...qkv_proj`.

This PR keeps the indexer out of the mapping that quant configs see, and fuses it into `qkv_proj` only when both resolve to the same quant method.

## Claims

- Checkpoints with quantized q/k/v and a BF16 indexer load again, for example `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ`. Their indexer runs as its own GEMM, as before #59533.
- No change for BF16, ModelOpt FP4, and checkpoints that treat q/k/v and the indexer the same way: the indexer stays fused.
- The `--enable-lora` mapping override is removed. It is no longer needed, and it never reached the quant config.

## Validation

End to end on 4x A100-PCIE-40GB (TP4 + EP) with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image built from `1b2a666` (2026-10-18). Its `model.py` and `qsa.py` match this PR's base `371745e`; for "after", the two files from this PR were mounted over them. A test-only hook (not part of this PR) logged the fusion decision of every QSA layer.

| Checkpoint | Code | Server start | QSA layers (12 per worker, 4 workers) | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AWQ` (q/k/v W4A16, indexer BF16) | before | fails: `ValueError: Found different quantization schemes ... layers.3.self_attn.qkv_proj` | - | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 unfused: `QKVParallelLinear` (`CompressedTensorsWNA16`) + BF16 `index_qk_proj` | GSM8K 86.2% (n=500), 0 invalid |
| `cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-AWQ-INT4` (attention BF16) | before | ok | 48/48 fused (`Qwen4ExpQSAQKVIndexerLinear`) | - |
| same | after | ok | 48/48 fused, same layer and quant method | sample request ok |

Both GPU runs used an earlier revision of the fusion check. The final check makes the same decision for both checkpoints: different quant methods for Swift, the same for cyankiwi.

GSM8K (an API key header was added by a small wrapper):

```bash
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8002 --use-chat-completions \
  --model swift-1.5-flash-next-awq --reasoning-effort none --num-shots 0 \
  --num-questions 500 --max-tokens 512 --temperature 0 --max-concurrency 32
```

The default 5-shot completions mode does not suit this model family: it emits EOS right after `Answer:` once the prompt is longer than about 400 tokens, on vLLM and on llama.cpp alike.

- Unit test (CPU): `test_qkv_proj_mapping_allows_bf16_indexer` in `tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py`. With the old mapping, both cases fail with the error from #62308.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: passed.
- CI: the test runs in the existing CPU Qwen4 Exp step (`qwen4-exp-unit-tests-cpu`). CI has no Flash-Next checkpoint with this layout (about 165 GB), so the end-to-end load is validated only as above.

## Details

- Root cause: `configure_quant_config` passes the class-level `packed_modules_mapping` to the quant config before `__init__` runs. Even the plain `QKVParallelLinear` built before fusion is resolved as a four-shard layer. The LoRA branch rebinds the mapping on the instance, so the quant config never saw it.
- Change:
  - `packed_modules_mapping["qkv_proj"]` is `["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"]` for both model classes.
  - `Qwen4ExpQSAAttention` builds q/k/v and the indexer as before, then fuses only if both resolve to the same quant method type. Without a quant config for the fused layer (BF16, or ModelOpt FP4 via `without_modelopt_fp4`) it fuses as before.
- Limitation: if q/k/v and the indexer are both quantized with the same quant method but a different scheme or parameters (bits or group size), they are still fused, and loading fails at weight loading. I have not seen a checkpoint with this layout.
- I used AI assistance (Claude) for the investigation, the code and the tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

```
  --stream-interval 10 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --enable-auto-tool-choice --trust-remote-code
```

commits.pr_title: [CI] Shard draft decoding, Qwen eval and scheduling automatically
commits.pr_body:

## Overview

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSv4/4.1] Fuse inverse RoPE and MXFP8 quant into the aiter sparse MLA and sparse MLA gating changes
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm with the aiter sparse MLA backend, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 ran a separate `rocm_inverse_rope_rows_` pass (and, on V4.1, a separate MXFP8 quantization) after attention. The aiter kernel can now do both in its store, so this passes it the positions / cos-sin cache (and the MXFP8 output buffer) and drops the extra passes.

- DSv4.1: decode and prefill rotate in the store; with an MXFP8 `o_proj` input the store also quantizes into it.
- DSv4: decode and prefill rotate in the store when `wo_a` is BF16. The fp8 `wo_a` path is unchanged (`inverse_rope_group_quant` already rotates there).
- Rows not rotated by a kernel store still go through the standalone pass (none on the aiter path).
- Also, gluon sparse MLA path is disabled for num_heads > 64 + prefill. For those workloads, existing kv gather + OPUS is faster.

Requires the aiter change adding `inv_rope_positions`, `inv_rope_cos_sin_cache` and `out_mxfp8` to `sparse_mla_fwd`, merge after the aiter bump (already done, aiter v0.1.25 has the support for these changes).

Perf. and accuracy runs to be added.

## Details
### Performance

### Fast Agent-X performance
Using AIPERF_EXPERIMENTAL_FAST=1 and agentx recipes for the selected config points. It is 20 min version of the full agentx benchmark.
This section compares turning VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA on/off.
  **DSV41-Flash**
| point | interactivity | P90 interactivity | output tok/s/GPU | TTFT | TPOT (on vs off) |

## Justification for the Switch point for num_heads=64, DSV4
### Prefill

Based on this data, when we have 128 heads, gathering/dequantizing KV cache from scaled fp8 to bf16 first then doing attention in BF16 without dequant and paging is faster.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Moves three steps that split their tests by hand onto `automatic_shard`, following #62077 and #62084. `kernels-b200` ran a hand-written `case "$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB"` block per shard. The two MoE Refactor integration steps read a different config list in each shard (`config-*-shard-$$BUILDKITE_PARALLEL_JOB.txt`). Each now runs plain pytest, the planner splits it using main's timings, and new tests or configs no longer need placing in a shard by hand.

## Claims

| Step | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---:|---:|
| `kernels-b200` | 3 hand-written `case` shards | 3 |
| `moe-refactor-integration-test-b200-temporary` | 4 config-list shards | 6 |
| `moe-refactor-integration-test-h100-temporary` | 4 config-list shards | 4 |

- Every test and every config runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment as before.
- A test file or config added later is placed by the planner, not by editing a `case` arm or a shard list.
- Labels drop `Shard %N`; the generator names jobs `<label> shard N/M`.
- The AMD mirrors (NVFP4 Dense Emulation, both MoE Refactor mirrors) are short. They stop inheriting the fixed shards and run as one job each.

## Validation

- Planned each step with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this branch and main's timings.
- Rendered each step with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper. Every test of every command ran in exactly one shard, with the same env (6/6 cases).
- For the config-list steps, also ran the generated shard jobs against vLLM's real `tests/evals/gsm8k/conftest.py` and config files, with the test body stubbed. All 19 B200 configs and all 12 H100 configs ran once each across the shards. No shard printed `not in the plan`, so the plan matched every config ID that main has timings for.
- `/ci run` [97474](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97474), rebased on main after ci-infra#836:
  - `kernels-b200` passed in 3 shards. Its 28 pytest runs total 2640 passed, 504 skipped and 1424 deselected, the same as main [97527](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97527); machine time in line with main.
  - The MoE Refactor B200 step passed in 6 shards and the H100 step in 4, with all 19 B200 and all 12 H100 configs passing once each, as on main. Machine time is in line with main for both.
  - All three AMD mirrors passed as one job each.

## Details

- **`kernels-b200` setup.** `python3 examples/basic/offline_inference/chat.py` was in shard 1 only. The planner needs plain pytest after the first pytest command, so it now runs as a setup command, once in each shard.
- **Config lists.** `moe-refactor/config-b200.txt` already listed exactly the union of the four B200 shard lists. `config-h100.txt` is the union of the four H100 shard lists. The per-shard lists are removed.
- **ROCm list kept twice.** The H100 step's AMD mirror now reads a new combined `config-rocm.txt`. `config-rocm-shard-*.txt` stay because the separate `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` still reads them.
- **`moe-refactor-integration-test-h100-temporary`.** Before ci-infra#836 the planner gave it 3 shards that ran longer than the old fixed shards. With each job's setup now in the budget it plans 4, each under the 20-minute target.
- **Timeouts unchanged (human).** As in #62077 and #62084, `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job. A single-job fallback (no plan, or the `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` rollback switch) would outrun it. Fallback-aware timeouts belong in a central timeout setting.
- **Left out.** `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` and `lora-tp-distributed` move in #62537, and `basic-models-tests-extra-initialization` in #63907. `spec-decode-mtp-other-acceptance-nightly` and the Humming A100/H100 steps stay on fixed shards: their fixed shards are already as short as a plan can make them, or they have no timings.

commits.pr_body: ## Overview Python logs generated outputs when `--enable-log-outputs` is set, on chat, completions (vllm-project/vllm#62205) and raw generate, with `--enable-log-deltas` (default true) controlling the per-update lines. The Rust frontend declared both flags as unsupported placeholders, so `vllm serve --enable-log-requests --enable-log-outputs` with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1` failed at startup. This PR implements both. Supersedes inactive vllm-project/vllm#57186 (chat only, last commit 2026-09-17). ## Claims - `--enable-log-outputs` and `--enable-log-deltas` are real Rust frontend flags, also accepted through `--args-json`. As in Python, `--enable-log-outputs` requires `--enable-log-requests`. - With them, Rust logs one line per streamed update (when deltas are on) and one complete line per choice on chat and completions, and the output token IDs on non-streaming raw generate. commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Keep completions top_logprobs and prompt_logprobs in the engine's order like Python
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Python builds each legacy completions `top_logprobs` entry, and each `prompt_logprobs` entry, as a dict over the engine's logprobs row, so the JSON keys come in the engine's order with the sampled (or prompt) token first. Rust collected both into a `HashMap`, so key order varied between identical requests. This PR keeps the engine's order. One commit per surface. ## Claims - Completions `top_logprobs` keys, and `prompt_logprobs` keys on chat and completions, come out in the engine's order with the sampled or prompt token first, as in Python. - A repeated key keeps its first position and takes the last value, which is Python's dict semantics. - This unblocks the completions cases of `tests/entrypoints/openai/test_return_tokens_as_ids.py`, which read the first key of each echoed `top_logprobs` entry as the prompt token (`next(iter(...))`). ## Validation Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root: ``` cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check # ok cargo sort --workspace --check rust # ok cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # ok cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings # ok cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast # 2312 tests run: 2312 passed, 13 skipped ``` The first commit alone also passes workspace clippy and nextest. - `completion_top_logprobs_keep_engine_order`: engine row `[C, A, B, C]` gives `{"C","A","B"}`, for strings and for `token_id:N`. - `prompt_logprobs_maps_keep_engine_order`: keys `[3, 1, 2]`. - Both fail with `HashMap` and pass with the fix. ## Details Python: `append_logprobs_for_next_position` (`vllm/logprobs.py`), then the dict comprehension in `_create_completion_logprobs` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/serving.py:774-791`). Change: `LogProbs.top_logprobs` and `PromptLogprobs` (`rust/src/server/src/routes/openai/utils/types.rs`) hold `IndexMap`s, collected in the engine row's order. `IndexMap`'s `FromIterator` already keeps a repeated key at its first position with the last value, so no extra dedup is needed. The workspace `indexmap` dependency gains its `serde` feature; no new crate. The order is a property of the wire DTOs, whose only producers are the two converters in `utils/logprobs.rs`. The decoded entries from `vllm-text` already arrive in engine order, so only the DTO's map type changes. Not a duplicate: no open PR changes the Rust logprobs map type. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01K2SEJPm2Mawmm6pu8m9E1o ---

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Forward profiler_kwargs from /start_profile
commits.pr_body:
## Overview vllm-project/vllm#51974 added `profiler_kwargs` to `POST /start_profile`: Python forwards it to the engine's `profile` utility, which merges it into the torch profiler kwargs. The Rust route had no such field, so serde ignored it and the engine profiled with its configured defaults. This PR forwards it. ## Claims - `POST /start_profile` on the Rust frontend accepts `profiler_kwargs` (a JSON object) and passes it unchanged as the fifth argument of the engine `profile` utility call, `nil` when absent, as Python sends `None`. - Like Python, the frontend does not interpret the keys. ## Validation Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root: ``` cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check # ok cargo sort --workspace --check rust # ok cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # ok cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings # ok cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast # 2310 tests run: 2310 passed, 13 skipped ``` - `start_profile_route_forwards_session_overrides` now sends `profiler_kwargs` and asserts that the msgpack `profile` call to the scripted mock engine carries it as the fifth argument; it fails when the route passes `None` instead. - The no-override tests assert the fifth argument is `nil` (shared `profile_start_without_overrides` helper). ## Details Python path: the route forwards `StartProfileRequest.model_dump(exclude_none=True)` to `AsyncLLM.start_profile`, which calls the `profile` utility as `(True, profile_prefix, delay_iterations, max_iterations, profiler_kwargs)` (`vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py`); `EngineCore.profile` hands it to the executor, and `vllm/profiler/wrapper.py` merges it. Rust: `StartProfileRequest` (`rust/src/server/src/routes/profile.rs`) gains the field, and `EngineCoreClient::start_profile` sends it as the fifth argument. The route DTO owns the field and `vllm-engine-core-client` owns the utility's wire arguments, so the value travels along the existing `start_profile` path with one added parameter and no new validation. Known difference, unchanged here: a wrongly typed override (`"profiler_kwargs": "invalid"`) gets Rust's JSON-body 400 where Python returns 422, as for the other three fields. `tests/entrypoints/serve/test_profile_api_router.py` is in-process and cannot run against the Rust frontend. Not a duplicate: no open PR touches the Rust `/start_profile` route. commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Moves `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` and `lora-tp-distributed`, with their AMD mirrors, from hand-written fixed shards to `automatic_shard`. Both were left out of #62120 until the L4 queue was back so they could be validated.

## Claims

| Step | Was | Planned shards |
|---|---|---:|
| `distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` | 3 fixed (`case` block) | 3 |
| `amd-distributed-model-tests-2-gpus` | 3 fixed (`case` block) | 4 |
| `lora-tp-distributed` | 4 fixed (`test ... \|\|` guards) | 3 |
| `amd-lora-tp-distributed` | 4 fixed (`if ...; fi` guards) | 3 |

- Every test runs exactly once across the shards, with the same environment and `-m` filters as before.
- A test file added later is placed by the planner rather than by editing a `case` branch.

## Validation

- Planned each step and mirror with ci-infra main's `runtime_shard.plan_step` against this branch and main's timings; every planned shard is well under the 20-minute target.
- Rendered each step and mirror with the pipeline generator and ran every shard's commands against a mock test tree, as a PR build and with main's `pytest -p ci_otel` wrapper: every test of every command ran in exactly one shard, with the same env (4/4 NVIDIA cases, 4/4 AMD mirror cases).
- `/ci run` [97471](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97471), rebased on main after ci-infra#836: every shard of both steps and both mirrors passed, with passed/skipped totals equal to main ([97556](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97556), [97527](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97527)). The NVIDIA steps' machine time is in line with main. The AMD mirrors' shards ran a few minutes longer than the same plans did before the rebase ([96709](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96709)): every job that day spent longer starting up before its first command, and its tests ran slower too. The Distributed Models mirror's slowest shard still finished well ahead of main's slowest fixed shard that day.

## Details

- **Commands.** Each `case` branch or guarded line becomes one plain command. The AMD mirror's `&&` chains become separate commands; a failing command still fails the job.
- **Timeouts unchanged (human).** As in #62077 and #62120, `timeout_in_minutes` stays per job. A single-job fallback (no plan, or the `VLLM_CI_RUNTIME_SHARD` rollback switch) would outrun it; fallback-aware timeouts belong in a central timeout setting.
- **Left out.** The separate `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` copy of the Distributed Models mirror keeps its fixed shards.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][DSpark] Stack DeepSeek V41 context WKV projections
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Replace DeepSeek-V4.1 DSpark’s per-layer context Q+KV projections with one stacked KV-only projection. The existing context path computes Q values that are immediately discarde

refer to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54674

## Claims

- Compute context KV for all draft layers with one MergedColumnParallelLinear.
- Reuse the existing V4 weight-duplication helper to load each layer’s WKV weights and scales into the stacked projection.


## Validation

### microbenchmark

<details>
<summary> script </summary>

```
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
"""Compare V4.1 DSpark context projection, normalization and cache insertion.

Uses checkpoint WQA/WKV/RMSNorm weights and synthetic BF16 hidden states.
The baseline source must expose the original DSparkDeepseekV4Model method.
Humming uses its production heuristics in both arms; no tuning overrides.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import statistics
from functools import partial
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
from safetensors import safe_open

from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from vllm.config.kernel import IrOpPriorityConfig
from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.humming import HummingMxfp8LinearKernel
from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.Mxfp8LinearKernel import (
    Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig,
)
from vllm.model_executor.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia import dspark

K, Q, V, LAYERS = 5120, 1280, 512, 3


class Projection(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, weight, scale, parts):
        super().__init__()
        self.input_size = K
        self.output_partition_sizes = parts
        self.params_dtype = torch.bfloat16
        self.has_bias = False
        self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(weight.cuda(), requires_grad=False)
        self.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
            scale.view(torch.uint8)
            .repeat_interleave(32, dim=0)
            .cuda()
            .view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu),
            requires_grad=False,
        )
        self.kernel = HummingMxfp8LinearKernel(
            Mxfp8LinearLayerConfig(weight_shape=tuple(weight.shape))
        )
        self.kernel.process_weights_after_loading(self)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.kernel.apply_weights(self, x)


def benchmark(args):
    torch.manual_seed(42)
    index = json.loads((args.checkpoint / "model.safetensors.index.json").read_text())[
        "weight_map"
    ]

    def read(name):
        with safe_open(args.checkpoint / index[name], framework="pt") as f:
            return f.get_tensor(name)

    old = []
    kv_weights, kv_scales, norms = [], [], []
    for i in range(LAYERS):
        prefix = f"mtp.{i}.attn."
        qw, qs = read(prefix + "wq_a.weight"), read(prefix + "wq_a.scale")
        vw, vs = read(prefix + "wkv.weight"), read(prefix + "wkv.scale")
        old.append(Projection(torch.cat([qw, vw]), torch.cat([qs, vs]), [Q, V]))
        kv_weights.append(vw)
        kv_scales.append(vs)
        norm = RMSNorm(V, eps=1e-20, dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda()
        norm.weight.data.copy_(read(prefix + "kv_norm.weight"))
        norms.append(norm)
    merged = Projection(torch.cat(kv_weights), torch.cat(kv_scales), [V] * LAYERS)
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.dspark_baseline", args.baseline_source
    )
    baseline = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(baseline)
    report = {
        "gpu": torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "checkpoint": str(args.checkpoint),
        "source_sha256": {
            "A": hashlib.sha256(args.baseline_source.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
            "B": hashlib.sha256(Path(dspark.__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        },
        "boundary": "3-layer context projection + RMSNorm + RoPE/quant/cache insert",
        "timing": "CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2, ABBA, median of round medians",
        "input": "Synthetic BF16 hidden states; actual checkpoint weights/scales",
        "compute_config": merged.kernel.compute_config,
        "tuning": "Both arms warmed; unchanged production Humming heuristics",
        "correctness": "Normalized KV atol=0.02, rtol=0.02; cache bytes may differ",
        "rows": [],
    }
    for m in args.tokens:
        x = torch.randn(m, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        positions = torch.arange(m, device="cuda")
        rope = torch.zeros(m, 64, device="cuda")
        rope[:, :32] = 1
        models = []
        for _ in range(2):
            layers = []
            for i in range(LAYERS):
                attn = SimpleNamespace(
                    fused_wqa_wkv=lambda x, i=i: (old[i](x), None),
                    q_lora_rank=Q,
                    kv_norm=norms[i],
                    kv_mxfp8=True,
                    rotary_emb=SimpleNamespace(cos_sin_cache=rope),
                    swa_cache_layer=SimpleNamespace(
                        block_size=64,
                        kv_cache=torch.zeros(
                            (m + 63) // 64, 64, 528, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8
                        ),
                    ),
                )
                layers.append(SimpleNamespace(attn=attn))
            models.append(
                SimpleNamespace(
                    layers=layers,
                    context_wkv_proj=merged,
                    num_dspark_layers=LAYERS,
                    config=SimpleNamespace(head_dim=V),
                )
            )
        modules = [baseline, dspark]
        functions = [
            partial(
                module.DSparkDeepseekV4Model.precompute_and_store_context_kv,
                model,
                x,
                positions,
                [positions] * LAYERS,
            )
            for module, model in zip(modules, models)
        ]
        for _ in range(20):
            for function in functions:
                function()
        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

        normalized = []
        for module, function in zip(modules, functions):
            outputs = []
            with patch.object(
                module,
                "_insert_context_kv",
                lambda attn, kv, p, s, out=outputs: out.append(kv.clone()),
            ):
                function()
            normalized.append(torch.stack(outputs, dim=1))
        torch.testing.assert_close(normalized[1], normalized[0], rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)
        max_abs = (normalized[1].float() - normalized[0].float()).abs().max().item()
        samples = {"A": [], "B": []}
        for arm in "ABBA":
            times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
                functions[arm == "B"], use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True
            )
            samples[arm].append(statistics.median(times) * 1000)
        a, b = [statistics.median(samples[arm]) for arm in "AB"]
        row = {
            "tokens": m,
            "A_us": a,
            "B_us": b,
            "latency_reduction_pct": (1 - b / a) * 100,
            "speedup": a / b,
            "normalized_kv_max_abs": max_abs,
            "round_median_us": samples,
            "useful_kv_projection_tflops_A": 2 * m * K * LAYERS * V / (a * 1e6),
            "useful_kv_projection_tflops_B": 2 * m * K * LAYERS * V / (b * 1e6),
        }
        report["rows"].append(row)
        print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    report["status"] = "completed"
    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--baseline-source", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[8, 48, 1024, 16384])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    priority = IrOpPriorityConfig.with_default(

    )
    with (
        torch.inference_mode(),
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Avoid double rounding in fused MoE expand
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix FP16 residual accumulation in the fused MoE LoRA fallback on XPU, without changing tests or tolerances. CUDA and ROCm keep their previous accumulation behavior.

## Claims

- Keep the XPU expand accumulator and residual sum in FP32, converting only when storing the result.
- Preserve the existing dtype conversion and addition order for non-XPU backends.
- Addresses the precision path introduced by #59931 without changing shared behavior on CUDA/ROCm.

## Validation

- Atomic-add cast cleanup: `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k large_rank_fallback` — 16 passed; file-level pre-commit passed. A direct `SPLIT_K=2` shrink check also matched the FP32 reference exactly for binary-scaled FP16/BF16 inputs on XPU.
- After removing the redundant cast before `tl.store`: `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py` — 433 passed in 309.11s on two Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs; original tests/tolerances unchanged. CUDA was unavailable.
- `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=6,7 /work/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/lora/test_fused_moe_lora_kernel.py -k test_fused_moe_lora_kernel_large_rank_fallback` — 16 passed on Intel Arc Pro B60.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/triton_ops/fused_moe_lora_op.py` — passed.
- The CI BMG-specific numerical discrepancy was not reproduced on local B60; Intel CI is still needed to validate that hardware-specific case.

## Details

The XPU specialization keeps the FP32 dot accumulator through residual addition so the LoRA result is not rounded to FP16 before adding the residual. It is selected only for XPU expand calls; shrink and all non-XPU calls retain the existing conversion order. No test code or tolerance was modified.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Qwen4Exp] Reserve QSA indexer prefill workspace during memory profiling
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reserve the Qwen4Exp QSA indexer's selection scratch (prefill logits workspace, or the worst-case decode logits,
whichever is larger) during the memory-profiling run, so the KV pool is not sized past what the indexer needs at
runtime. Fixes #60489.

## Claims

- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4Exp`) no longer OOMs inside `qsa_select_paged_prefill` on the first long prefill
  when `--max-model-len` and `--gpu-memory-utilization` are high: the profiler now accounts for the indexer
  logits workspace (`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, 512 MiB by default) plus the 1 MiB top-k workspace.
- Configurations that genuinely do not fit are rejected at startup with the existing actionable
  "estimated maximum model length" error instead of failing at request time.
- The decode path is covered too: `qsa_select_paged_decode` allocates `[decode tokens, compressed columns]` fp32
  logits on demand, which exceeds the 512 MiB prefill budget above 2048 decode tokens per step at 262K (e.g.
  `max_num_seqs` 1024 with MTP K=3). The reservation is `max(prefill budget, worst-case decode logits)` plus the
  top-k workspace, like `sparse_attn_indexer`.
- ~25 lines in the QSA profiling branch (`vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/qsa.py`); no core/runner changes.

## Validation

`Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound`, 4× RTX 3090 (SM86), TP=4 + EP, nightly `0.30.1rc1.dev702`
(this file set is unchanged on current `main`):

```bash
vllm serve Intel/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-W4A16-AutoRound --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 262144 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.96 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --max-num-seqs 32 --cpu-offload-gb 2 --cpu-offload-params visual
# then one ~250K-token chat request
```

| default 512 MiB indexer budget | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV memory / GPU | 3.32 GiB | 2.93 GiB (workspace accounted) |
| Startup | succeeds | fails fast: "estimated maximum model length is 236400. Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization` …" |
| First long prefill | OOM in `qsa_select_paged_prefill` (512 MiB requested, 168 MiB free)¹ | n/a (rejected up front) |

¹ Reproduced with `--language-model-only` in place of the two offload flags (3.49 GiB KV/GPU), same OOM site.

With `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=128` the fixed build starts at 262K and the profiler's numbers hold at
runtime: a c=1/8/32 decode sweep and a 300-question GSM8K/MMLU-Pro eval run with no OOM; in a build that also
carried #60491 (fp8_e5m2 KV) and the #53981 rebase, two 250K-token passkey requests (depth 0.5 and 0.1) pass. Output is unaffected (the change only runs in the profiling branch).

Decode worst case (eager decode, no CUDA graphs, `--language-model-only`, `--max-num-seqs 128`,
`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB=16` so decode dominates), instrumented with a test-only log line:

| | first commit (prefill only) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Reserved during profiling | 16 MiB + 1 MiB | **33,587,200 B** + 1 MiB (formula) |
| Real decode logits at runtime (128 concurrent requests) | up to 31,225,600 B (119 rows × 65,600 cols), **not reserved** | ≤ 33,587,200 B (128 × 65,600), covered |
| KV pool / c=128 load / 250K passkey | 283,825 tokens / pass | 283,825 tokens / pass (×2 runs) / pass |

The formula's worst-case width (`cdiv(max_model_len, block_size) × cdiv(block_size, compress_ratio)` = 65,600 at
262K, block size 1600) matched the runtime decode logits exactly. The old version did not OOM here (the 16 MB
shortfall fit in allocator slack); at larger `max_num_seqs` × speculative tokens the shortfall grows into
hundreds of MB. The final inlined code was re-run in the same config: identical KV pool, c=128 ×2, c=1/8/32 sweep
and a 250K passkey all pass with no OOM.

`pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD`: all hooks pass.

No unit test added: the behaviour is the profiler's view of peak GPU memory during the dummy run, which a CPU
unit test cannot observe; CI has no Qwen3.8-Flash-Next long-context job. Validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: the profiling dummy run carries no attention metadata, so `Qwen4ExpQSA.forward` takes the
`not isinstance(metadata, dict)` branch and returns before the indexer runs. `qsa_select_paged_prefill`
allocates its logits workspace on demand ("always allocate the worst case"), so the profiler never sees it.
The generic `sparse_attn_indexer` already handles the same situation with a dummy allocation of
`max(decode logits, prefill cap)` in its own no-metadata branch; this mirrors that inline in the QSA profiling
branch (review feedback: inlined rather than a single-use helper). QSA attention runs eagerly outside CUDA-graph
capture (`@eager_break_during_capture`), so the reservation never lands in a graph pool.

Tradeoff, by design: the KV pool shrinks by the memory the indexer really needs (~0.4 GiB/GPU here at the
default budget). Users can trade that back by lowering `VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`; the indexer chunks
rows to fit. The reservation is freed immediately and only runs during profiling, so there is no steady-state
cost and no added host/device synchronization.

Duplicate check: searched open issues/PRs for the QSA indexer/profiling area (`qsa indexer`,
`VLLM_SPARSE_INDEXER_MAX_LOGITS_MB`, `qsa_select_paged_prefill`); no existing report or fix.

AI assistance: this change, the investigation and the description were prepared with an AI coding assistant
(Claude Code). I reviewed the diff and ran the validation above on my own hardware.
