commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Apply the draft max_model_len limit before model config hooks
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #63844. On Model Runner V2, a hybrid Mamba/attention target with prefix caching disabled and a draft whose `max_model_len` is below the target's fails config validation with `--mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching`, although the flag was never set. Regression from #63251.

## Claims

- `VllmConfig` now lowers `max_model_len` to the draft's before running the model `verify_and_update_config` hooks, so values they derive from it (here the default `mamba_block_size`) use the final length.
- The reported command starts on V2; V1 and non-hybrid models are unchanged.

## Validation

New test `test_draft_limit_applies_before_hybrid_mamba_block_size` goes through `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`, the path shared by `LLM` and `vllm serve` (CPU, only config files are fetched).

Before (fix reverted):

```text
$ pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_limits_max_model_len.py -k hybrid
E       pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for VllmConfig
E         Value error, --mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching
1 failed, 4 deselected
```

After:

```text
$ pytest tests/config/test_speculative_draft_limits_max_model_len.py tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py
20 passed
```

Wider suite `pytest tests/config tests/test_config.py` (macOS, CPU-only, `test_ray_runtime_env` deselected since Ray isn't installed): 771 passed, 29 failed. All 29 fail identically on `main` without this change (gated `meta-llama` repos, model inspection failing for multimodal architectures on this platform, CPU-specific compilation defaults, and V1-runner async-scheduling checks), so none are introduced here.

End to end, the reproducer from #63844 (`--load-format dummy`, CPU) now passes config validation; before the fix it raised the error above from `create_engine_config`:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-random --max-model-len 4096 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --load-format dummy \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"draft_model","model":"ai21labs/Jamba-tiny-random","num_speculative_tokens":3,"max_model_len":1024}'
```

The test runs in the CPU "Multimodal + Config" Buildkite step (`pytest -v -s config`, depends on `vllm/config/`). `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

## Details

Root cause: #63251 added `_limit_max_model_len_to_draft()` after `try_verify_and_update_config()`. For hybrid models with prefix caching off, `MambaModelConfig.verify_and_update_config` sets `mamba_block_size = max_model_len` (4096). The limit then lowers `max_model_len` to 1024, and the after-validator `validate_mamba_block_size` reads `mamba_block_size != max_model_len` as a user-set flag.

Moving the limit ahead of the hooks is safe: it only reads the speculative config and `use_v2_model_runner`, which depends on `speculative_config`, `lora_config`, and `parallel_config` fields (executor backend, PP/DCP/PCP sizes, ubatching) that the hooks do not write. Hooks that also lower `max_model_len` (e.g. the 8192 cap for EmbeddingGemma2) still apply, now on top of the draft limit, so the result is the same minimum. Other values the hooks derive from `max_model_len`, such as `rotary_kwargs["max_position"]`, also see the final length now.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #63844 or `_limit_max_model_len_to_draft`. #52045 works around the same validator for a different trigger (CPU MLA disabling prefix caching) and does not touch this ordering.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4] Give zero and subnormal mono MXFP8 groups vLLM's scale code
commits.pr_body: - `stages/moe.py` (`vllm_mx_code`) and `attention/device.py` (`mx_code`) in the DeepSeek-V4 and V4.1 mono decode kernels: when `q = RN(max(amax, FLT_MIN) / 448)` is an f32 subnormal, return code 0 for `q <= 2^-127` and 1 above it, instead of the exponent-bit result, which is always 1 The four copies take the E8M0 scale code from the exponent bits of `q`. Their docstrings, and vLLM's `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`, give `clamp(ceil(log2 q) + 127, 0, 254)`. For a subnormal `q` the bit trick gives 1, so every group with `amax <= 448 * 2^-127`, including all-zero groups, gets code 1 where vLLM gives 0. The monokernel I/O tests in #63486 catch this, and it blocks that PR. In practice, zero groups (for example a zeroed norm-weight group) only get a different scale byte and still dequantize to 0. bf16-valued inputs never dequantize differently. Only the f32 attention-output quant (XO) could, for groups with amax below 2.6e-36. | amax | q | before | after | vLLM rule (Triton / torch op) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 0 | FLT_MIN / 448 | 1 | 0 | 0 / 0 | | 1e-36 | subnormal | 1 | 0 | 0 / 0 | | 448 * 2^-127 | 2^-127 | 1 | 0 | 0 / 0 | | prev(448 * 2^-126) | rounds to 2^-126 | 1 | 1 | 1 / 1 | | 1.0 | normal | 119 | 119 | 119 / 119 | | check (MI355X) | before | after | |---|---|---| | every non-negative finite f32 amax (2,139,095,040), each of the 4 copies | 73,400,322 wrong codes | 0 | | `test_mono_primitives.py -k scale_codes` (#63486) | 4 failed | 5 passed | | DSv4.1 layer test, hard case with a zeroed norm group | 48 of 7680 codes wrong per quant, 16/16 runs | 0, 10/10 runs | | f32-valued tiny groups, dequantized vs vLLM | 195,270 elements differ | 0 | Decode step time, 20-step CUDA graph, median of interleaved runs (DSv4.1 TP4: 10 runs per arm; DSv4-Pro TP8: pooled runs), with #63576 applied in every DSv4.1 arm: | case | before (us) | after (us) | delta | |---|---|---|---| | DSv4.1 1x1, index source | 75.94 | 76.66 | +0.94% | | DSv4.1 1x6, index source | 102.86 | 103.03 | +0.17% | | DSv4.1 8x6, index source | 314.73 | 314.95 | +0.07% | | DSv4.1 8x6, hard case | 170.75 | 170.67 | -0.05% | | DSv4-Pro 1x1 | 90.69 | 90.79 | +0.11% | | DSv4-Pro 1x7 | 124.45 | 124.41 | -0.03% | | DSv4-Pro 64x1 | 412.24 | 412.84 | +0.15% | An unchanged-code control arm moved -0.21% to +0.11% on DSv4-Pro and +0.10 us on DSv4.1. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Release the warmup memory cached on the capture streams
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Empty the caching allocator once at the end of the Model Runner V2 `capture_model()`, before it reads free memory, so that warmup activations cached on the discarded capture streams are released. Fixes #63052.

## Claims

- With breakable CUDA graphs and no FULL graphs (`cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`), the largest warmup's activations stay reserved on the capture stream for the life of the process and are reported as CUDA graph memory. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill (GB200, DP4) that is 10.49 GiB per rank; this PR releases it.
- Modes with FULL graphs already end in this state, because `torch.cuda.graph()` empties the cache before each FULL capture.
- 3 lines; graph pools and allocated memory are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill, DP4, `max_model_len` 1M, breakable graphs with capture sizes up to 16384 tokens, v0.32.0-based build. Per rank, at the end of `capture_model()`, with the default-pool segments of `torch.cuda.memory._snapshot()` grouped by stream:

| | `PIECEWISE` (`main`) | `PIECEWISE` + `empty_cache()` at the end | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (`main`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| model capture stream: reserved (in use) | 7.93 (1.77) GiB | 2.43 (1.77) GiB | 2.43 (1.77) GiB |
| replay capture stream: reserved (in use) | 6.65 (1.65) GiB | 1.70 (1.65) GiB | 1.70 (1.65) GiB |
| graph capture memory (free-memory delta) | 26.39 GiB | 15.90 GiB | 21.00 GiB |
| `memory_allocated()` at the end | 119.12 GiB | 119.12 GiB | 119.16 GiB |

- The first two columns differ by 10.49 GiB per rank, all of it cached warmup memory. The graph pools (5.63 + 5.18 GiB), the allocated memory, and a smoke test are the same in both.
- The middle column comes from a diagnostic run that calls `empty_cache()` at the same point, after taking the snapshot above. This exact commit has not been run on a GPU.
- `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` also captures 44 FULL decode graphs and 39 FULL DSpark graphs, so its total is higher; its capture streams end up in the same state as the middle column.

No test is added: the effect needs a breakable PIECEWISE capture whose warmup is large enough to matter, and CI has no runner for that configuration.

## Details

**Root cause.**

1. `capture_model()` empties the cache once before capturing, and reads free memory at the end without emptying it again.
2. Each `CudaGraphManager.capture()` enters `graph_capture()`, which creates a new stream, and runs every size eagerly once before capturing it. The caching allocator keeps the freed warmup blocks on that stream. Sizes are captured largest first, so the cache ends up holding the largest warmup's peak, and nothing allocates on that stream afterwards.
3. `capture_model()` runs under `freeze_gc_for_cudagraph_capture()`. While gc is frozen, breakable capture skips its per-descriptor `gc.collect()` + `empty_cache()` (#54646).
4. With FULL graphs, `torch.cuda.graph.__enter__` empties the cache before each FULL capture and releases these blocks as a side effect. With PIECEWISE only, nothing does.

The blocks are released only when some caching-allocator allocation fails and the allocator frees all cached blocks to retry. Allocations outside the caching allocator (NCCL, NVSHMEM, CUDA module loading) see the memory as used.

**KV budget.** `profile_cudagraph_memory()` measures `capture_model(profile_only=True)`, so the CUDA graph estimate subtracted from the KV budget also includes these blocks today; with this change it no longer does (from reading the code; the KV cache size was not measured). This complements #59368, which measures the graph pool for the estimate: with #59368 alone, the estimate would exclude this cache while the real capture still holds it.

**Tradeoff.** As noted in #50780, on a model whose profile run under-counts long-prefill activations, these cached blocks acted as reclaimable headroom. With this change that memory goes to the KV cache instead, which is the state `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` already ends in.

Related: #62965 (the decoder replay graphs' separate stream and pool).

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode][Sampling] Batch-sharded draft logits
commits.pr_body:
## Context
During batch-sharded sampling, the target logits are sharded along the token dimension. The requests are deterministically assigned to ranks using the formula: `req_state_idx % tp_size`. So during TP=4, rank 0 only samples (and in the case of spec decoding verifies) requests with state indices: 0, 4, 8, 12, ....

Currently, draft model-derived speculators allocate persistent draft logits tensors to hold all requests up to `max-num-seqs`, which is wasteful during batch-sharded sampling because only `max-num-seqs // TP` of those request logits are actually used by each rank. Sharding the draft logits can enable us to save GPU memory.

## This PR

Under batch-sharded sampling, each rank now allocates draft logits only for the requests it verifies. The draft logits cache shrinks from `max_num_seqs` rows to `cdiv(max_num_seqs, tp_size)` rows per rank, and the freed memory goes to the KV cache.

**Layout.** A request's draft logits live only on its owner rank, at row `req_state_idx // tp_size`. Two Triton helpers in `batch_shard.py` define the pair: `shard_owner` (`req_state_idx % num_shards`, the existing owner rule) and `shard_row` (`req_state_idx // num_shards`). Every write and read of the cache goes through them. With one shard both reduce to the current behavior and compile away.

**Writes.** Drafting stays replicated, so every rank still samples every draft token and no new collectives are added. Each rank writes only the rows it owns:
- `gumbel_sample` takes `logits_cache_num_shards` / `logits_cache_shard_idx` and masks its cache store to the owner rank. `DraftModelSpeculator.sample_draft` and DSpark's `_sample_logits` pass them through.
- DFlash2's `_cache_draft_logits_kernel`, which writes only the top-k candidate columns, applies the same mask.

**Reads.** `RejectionSampler` takes `draft_logits_num_shards`, and the rejection kernels index draft logits with `shard_row(req_state_idx, DRAFT_LOGITS_NUM_SHARDS)`.

**Allocation.** The cache moves from `DraftModelSpeculator.__init__` to `load_model`, so it is allocated once at its final size after the target and draft models are loaded. It is sharded when all of these hold:
- batch-sharded sampling is active for the target (`batch_sharded_sampling_enabled`, a new helper that the model runner also uses to create the `BatchSharder`),
- the speculator opts in via `supports_batch_sharded_draft_logits()`,
- no draft watermarker is configured.

The model runner passes `speculator.draft_logits_num_shards` to the `RejectionSampler`. It also asserts that a custom rejection sampler never receives a sharded cache.

**Speculators that opt in:** every one whose cache writes honor the owner mask.
- `TargetDependentARSpeculator`: Eagle, MTP, Gemma4.
- `StandaloneARSpeculator` and `MultiModuleMTPSpeculator`.
- `DFlashSpeculator`, and through it DSpark, XPress, DFlash2 and LiLiCorr.
- **Exception:** DSpark keeps the full cache when the draft model provides its own fused `sample_sequential` (the AMD DeepSeek-V4.1 path), because those kernels write the full-size cache.

**Memory freed per rank** (TP4, `max_num_seqs=256`, probabilistic drafts), from server startup logs:

| Target + draft | Draft logits cache, base → shard | KV cache memory, base → shard | KV cache tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark (K=5) | 0.31 → 0.08 GiB | 74.44 → 74.67 GiB | +0.31% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP (K=3) | 0.36 → 0.09 GiB | 150.69 → 150.96 GiB | +0.18% |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash (K=7) | 0.83 → 0.21 GiB | 145.77 → 146.39 GiB | +0.43% |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 (K=7, fp32 cache) | 1.66 → 0.41 GiB | 147.07 → 148.31 GiB | +0.85% |

## Benchmarks

No regression in accuracy or acceptance rate for any speculator that now writes batch-sharded draft logits.

**Setup:** 4x GB200, TP4, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, prefix caching off, natural EOS. Each pair ran 4 server boots in the order base, shard, shard, base. "base" is `--enable-batch-sharded-sampling` off and "shard" is on. Startup logs confirmed every shard boot sharded the draft logits cache on all 4 ranks.

- **GSM8K:** `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions. t0 is temperature 0, one run per boot. t1 is temperature 1 with 3 seeds per boot, 6 runs per arm. The Qwen models use chat completions with thinking disabled.
- **SPEED-Bench:** `low_entropy` subset, `throughput_2k` config, concurrency 64, 256 prompts, temperature 1, top_p 1.
- **Acceptance length** = 1 + accepted / drafts, from the server's Prometheus metrics.
- Each cell shows the mean over the arm's runs.

### GSM8K accuracy

| Target + draft | K | t0 base | t0 shard | t1 base | t1 shard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | 5 | 0.907 | 0.906 | 0.816 | 0.807 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | 3 | 0.969 | 0.970 | 0.968 | 0.967 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | 7 | 0.970 | 0.970 | 0.966 | 0.966 |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | 7 | 0.964 | 0.961 | 0.960 | 0.960 |

### Acceptance length

| Target + draft | GSM8K t0 base | GSM8K t0 shard | GSM8K t1 base | GSM8K t1 shard | SPEED-Bench base | SPEED-Bench shard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark | 3.554 | 3.540 | 3.275 | 3.283 | 3.546 | 3.556 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + MTP | 3.617 | 3.619 | 3.519 | 3.515 | 3.258 | 3.271 |
| Qwen3.6-27B + DFlash | 5.499 | 5.490 | 4.980 | 4.984 | 3.905 | 3.927 |
| Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 | 6.164 | 6.152 | 5.876 | 5.890 | 3.636 | 3.647 |

### SPEED-Bench noise check (Qwen3.6-27B + MTP)

Every pair read 0.3–0.6% higher acceptance on SPEED-Bench with sharding. To check whether that was real, I ran a third arm that shards verification but keeps the draft logits cache replicated. I ran each arm with top-k on and off, with 2 boots per arm.

| Arm | top_k=20 (model default) | top_k disabled |
|---|---|---|
| base | 3.266 | 3.268 |
| sharded verification, replicated draft logits | 3.263 | 3.262 |
| sharded verification, sharded draft logits | 3.263 | 3.261 |

The three arms match. Base alone ranged from 3.254 to 3.279 across boots, so the shift is boot-to-boot noise.

### Notes

- **DFlash2 GSM8K t0, 0.964 → 0.961:** a 4-question difference. At temperature 0, verification compares against the target argmax and never reads cached draft logits, so this can't come from this change.
- **DSV4.1 GSM8K t1, 0.816 → 0.807:** not significant (Welch p≈0.3). This model's t1 accuracy varies a lot from seed to seed (0.78–0.83).

## Overview

Document the GB300 Kimi-K3 AgentX lanes of [SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#4516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4516) (head `5a397acc`) in `recipes/models/moonshotai/Kimi-K3.yaml`: the refreshed TP8 + DCP8 xPyD lane (`kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dcp8-disagg`) and a new 3P1D lane with a DEP16 decode pool (`kimik3-fp4-gb300-dynamo-vllm-agentic-dspark-mooncake-dep16-disagg`). Both run on image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-e4a5b5537344b103ed10de7764378ef09604ef3d` (vLLM `0.32.1rc1.dev466+ge4a5b5537` in the run logs) with Dynamo `a0de541ea8c861d5ac01d15953ca529bea68637b`.

## Claims

**`gb300_agentx_pd` (AgentX xPyD, default):**

- Image and Dynamo pin moved from `nightly-1b2a6663` / `ffbbaaa6` to the ones above.
- Both roles: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95` (was 0.92), `TOKENSPEED_MLA_FP16_PARTIALS=0`; `VLLM_CONNECTOR_PREFETCH_DEPTH` and `VLLM_CONNECTOR_PREFETCH_KV_CAP` removed (the lane no longer sets them).
- Prefill: `--max-num-seqs 32` (was 64), `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 8192` with an explicit `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` capture list up to 8192, and `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_LIMIT=1024` / `DYN_BACKEND_ADMISSION_ENGINE_REQUEST_WAITING_LIMIT=1024`.
- Runbook: the regular decode adds `--use-replayssm` (the specialized decode does not use it), the Mooncake store connector drops `compact_group_io` and `max_load_batch_keys`, and the frontend runs `--router-session-affinity-ttl-secs 1` (was 900) with `DYN_DISABLE_OPENAI_STRICT_SCHEMA_VALIDATION=1`. The worker table is unchanged (1P2D c56 is no longer run; c48 and c64 remain).

**`gb300_agentx_pd_dep16` (AgentX 3P1D DEP16, new, opt-in):**

- Prefill: TP8 + EP8 across two trays (no DCP), three workers; decode: one DEP16 worker (`--tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 16`, expert parallelism) across four trays. Both roles use MegaMoE, `--enable-ep-weight-filter`, `--max-num-seqs 32`, BF16 KDA state, FP8 KV and FlashInfer autotune.
- Online MXFP8 target quantization through `--quantization-config` `targets`: the KDA `in_proj_qkvgfab`, MLA `fused_qkv_a_g_proj` and latent-MoE `routed_expert_up_proj`/`routed_expert_down_proj` projections on both roles, plus `o_proj` and the shared experts on decode. The DSpark draft is not quantized: the draft is built from its own config (`get_draft_quant_config`), and the run logs show the online quantization pass only while the target loads.
- Decode: `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512`, `--use-replayssm`, `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv: 8`, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs (vLLM's default, replacing the DEP strategy's `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`), no prefix caching, and a Mooncake `kv_consumer` connector with `enable_lookup: false` (runbook).
- Runbook: services, environment (incl. the NVSHMEM MNNVL settings), prefill and decode commands, frontend.
- `meta.date_updated` bumped to 2026-10-26.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <this checkout>/recipes` passes (vllm-project/recipes @ `5eec681`).
- Built the full JSON API before and after: only the Kimi-K3 family files change (`moonshotai/Kimi-K3.json`, its `hw/gb300/strategies/pd_cluster.json` and `presets/gb300_agentx_pd.json`, the three promoted Kimi-K3 variants' index and GB300 PD files) and `presets/gb300_agentx_pd_dep16.json` is added. The GB300 PD default render changes only in the image and the flags and env vars listed above.
- Every value was taken from the PR-head recipes and checked against the dumped engine config of every worker in run [40239967341](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/40239967341) (all 8 disaggregated points): 1P3D c16 and 1P2D c24/c32 run the specialized decode (`--max-num-seqs 12`, capture 64, FP32 state, interleave 1, autotune off), 1P2D c48/c64, 2P3D c240 and 3P4D c240 run the regular decode (`--max-num-seqs 128`, `use_replayssm` on), every prefill runs `--max-num-seqs 32` with capture 8192 and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`, and the 3P1D c336 workers match the new preset. The rendered prefill/decode argv of both presets equal the lane's logged launch commands (c32 and c336) apart from the synthetic acceptance settings, `--kv-transfer-config`/`--kv-events-config` (runbook), node addresses, and builder flags that restate the lane's effective values: `--no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` (no HMA auto-disable in the logs), `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384` on the xPyD pools (the logs show `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`), and the xPyD preset's existing autotune, prefix-cache and hybrid-LB undo flags.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kimi K3] Opt-in KV-balanced FP8 MLA decode for agentic workloads
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds an opt-in MLA attention backend for Kimi-K3 on Blackwell, `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA`. Its decode splits each request's KV by its own length, so the decode stays balanced across the GPU when the context lengths in one batch differ a lot, as they do in agentic workloads. It is a standalone backend built on the common MLA backend classes (`MLACommonBackend`, `MLACommonImpl`, `MLACommonMetadataBuilder`); it does not depend on `TOKENSPEED_MLA`. The code lives in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kv_balanced_mla/`. Outside it, the PR only adds the backend's entry to `AttentionBackendEnum` (as the DeepSeek V4, MiniMax M3 and Step5 backends in `vllm/models/` have).

## Claims

- **Decode attention, AgentX context lengths on GB300:** 1.34–1.59x faster than `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`, and 1.91–2.67x faster than its default (geometric mean over batch sizes, DEP16 and DCP8, target verify and draft).
- **End-to-end, AgentX on GB300:**
  - DEP16 decode (3P1D c336): +7.8% TPS/GPU and +20% p90 interactivity.
  - DCP8 decode: +4.6% TPS/GPU and +10% p90 interactivity at 3P4D c240, and +2.7% / +13% at the prefill-bound 2P3D c240.
  - The baseline is `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`, the setting these recipes already use.
- **Accuracy:** gsm8k with real speculative rejection on the latest revision is 0.961 (DEP16) and 0.967 (DCP8).
- **Opt-in.** The backend is never selected automatically; without `--attention-backend KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` nothing changes.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kv_balanced_mla.py`, 12 tests, passing on GB300). They check the kernel against an FP32 reference for:
- unequal lengths and an empty request;
- the DSpark draft block (non-causal);
- a DCP8 shard on rank 0, and on rank 5 with interleave 64. The rank-5 lengths end inside that rank's chunks, so the causal mask cuts its last keys. Passing the wrong rank or interleave gives about 80% error, versus 2% when correct.
- a peaked softmax that fails without the P prescale;
- plan plus decode captured in a CUDA graph and replayed with KV lengths changed in place;
- a shared workspace larger than 2 GiB.

The backend tests check that `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` resolves to this backend, its builder and its base-2 LSE convention, and is in no platform's priority list; that selection rejects an FP16 model, a non-FP8 KV cache, a non-SM10x GPU and a `kv_lora_rank` other than 512; and that `forward_mqa` only runs the kernel. The decode tests check one plan per forward, the DCP path with the LSE, and that a step the kernel can't run raises a `ValueError`.

**Microbenchmark.** Time per decode step on one rank, from CUDA-graph replays, mean of 5 random batches per N. Context lengths are sampled from the AgentX trace (median about 98K tokens, p90 about 284K). Every variant decodes the same requests and was checked against an FP32 reference.
- `ts1` is `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with the default `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=1`.
- `ts8` is the same with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`.
- `kvb` is this PR's decode, excluding its plan. The plan takes 4–13 µs, runs once per forward and is shared by all MLA layers.

| Decode | Step | kvb vs ts1 | kvb vs ts8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16: 96 heads, full KV | verify (q=5, causal) | 2.63x (1.93–3.30) | 1.37x (1.25–1.54) |
| DEP16 | draft (64 heads, q=4) | 2.67x (1.17–4.39) | 1.34x (1.17–1.47) |
| DCP8: 96 gathered heads, 1/8 KV shard, LSE | verify | 1.91x (1.34–3.33) | 1.52x (1.41–1.70) |
| DCP8 | draft | 2.46x (1.78–3.32) | 1.59x (1.48–1.82) |

<details>
<summary>Per batch size (µs)</summary>

| Decode | Step | N | ts1 | ts8 | kvb | kvb vs ts1 | kvb vs ts8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEP16 | verify | 4 | 402.1 | 308.7 | 208.5 | 1.93x | 1.48x |
| DEP16 | verify | 8 | 928.3 | 433.6 | 281.1 | 3.30x | 1.54x |

| DCP8 | draft | 128 | 780.4 | 649.2 | 438.4 | 1.78x | 1.48x |

</details>

**End-to-end.**
- **Setup:** Kimi-K3 MXFP4 on GB300 NVL72, using the InferenceX AgentX agentic-coding replay with Dynamo disaggregated serving, Mooncake KV offload, and DSpark speculative decoding with 4 tokens (synthetic acceptance, as the recipes use).
- **Builds:** both sides run the same vLLM main build. The only difference is the decode workers' decode kernel. These runs used this PR's earlier revision, which selected the same kernel and dispatch through `additional_config` instead of the attention backend name. A rerun of the DEP16 point on the latest revision gave the same result.
- **Baseline:** the decode workers use `TOKENSPEED_MLA` with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv=8`.
- **Runs:** one run per side for each point. A repeat of the DEP16 pair gave +8.6% TPS/GPU.

| Config | TPS/GPU | Interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s) | E2E latency p90 | TTFT mean / p90 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3P1D, TP8 prefill + DEP16 decode, c336: baseline | 27,267 | 38.1 / 35.2 | 60.6 s | 3.14 / 5.82 s |
| same, KV-balanced | **29,402 (+7.8%)** | 45.8 / 42.4 (+20% / +20%) | 53.9 s (−11%) | 4.22 / 9.69 s |
| 3P4D, DCP8 prefill + DCP8 decode, c240: baseline | 20,421 | 75.7 / 68.9 | 33.3 s | 1.89 / 3.03 s |
| same, KV-balanced | **21,370 (+4.6%)** | 83.1 / 75.9 (+10% / +10%) | 30.8 s (−7%) | 1.84 / 2.94 s |
| 2P3D, DCP8 prefill + DCP8 decode, c240: baseline | 24,503 | 63.7 / 58.0 | 43.9 s | 5.21 / 10.74 s |
| same, KV-balanced | **25,162 (+2.7%)** | 72.6 / 65.3 (+14% / +13%) | 40.7 s (−7%) | 5.83 / 12.41 s |

- **Why TTFT rises at 3P1D and 2P3D:** a faster decode lets more requests through, which puts more load on the prefill workers that limit those points. At 3P4D, with more prefill capacity, TTFT improves slightly.
- **Why DCP8 gains less:** with DCP8, MLA attention is a smaller share of each decode step than with DEP16.

**Accuracy.** gsm8k (5-shot, lm-eval) with real speculative rejection, `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` on the decode workers (latest revision). Every decode step ran on the kernel.

| Config | strict-match | flexible-extract | Acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D, TP8 prefill + DEP16 decode | 0.961 | 0.961 | 3.61 |
| 1P1D, DCP8 prefill + DCP8 decode | 0.967 | 0.967 | 3.27 |

**CI.** The B200 Kimi K3 step (`models/kimi_k3`) runs the new tests. They were validated on GB300 (SM103) and not run on B200 (SM100). On the MI355 step the tests are skipped, and the test module imports without the CuTe kernel.

## Details

**KV imbalance in agentic decode.** An agentic decode batch mixes very different context lengths, for example 5K, 20K, 98K and 300K tokens. To spread one request's attention over the GPU, the decode cuts its KV into splits; clusters process the splits in parallel and a reduction merges them. `TOKENSPEED_MLA`, the existing FP8 MLA decode for this model, uses one split count for the whole batch: it's chosen from the batch size and SM count, with `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv` as a floor. With a skewed batch, any single count is wrong for most requests:
- **Too many splits for short requests.** Short requests are cut into tiny splits that each pay the per-split setup and the reduction.
- **Too few splits for long requests.** The longest requests leave a tail in which a few clusters stream hundreds of thousands of keys while the rest of the GPU is idle.

`min_split_kv=8` helps the long requests and hurts the short ones; at DCP8 N=128 it is slower than the default (see `ts8` vs `ts1`).

**What the KV-balanced decode does:**
1. **Plan.** A Triton planner gives each request its own split count from its KV length: 1 to 8 splits of at least 1024 tokens, sized to fill at most 8 waves of the GPU's clusters. It writes the planned (query tile, request, split) entries as a device work list. It reads nothing on the host, so it is captured in the decode CUDA graph. It runs once per forward, and every MLA layer reuses it.
2. **Execute.** One wave of persistent 2-CTA clusters walks the work list, so every cluster gets about the same amount of KV.
3. **Skip the merge where possible.** A request planned as a single split stores its final output directly, and the reduction skips it.
4. **Keep small probabilities.** Long splits can make probabilities small enough to flush to zero in E4M3, so P is stored scaled by 2^6 and the LSE removes the factor.

**Code layout** (`vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/kv_balanced_mla/`):
- `kernel.py` and `helpers.py`: TokenSpeed MLA 2.0.3's FP8 decode kernel (MIT), vendored with the changes above. Compared with the release, the kernel adds 347 lines (including renames and casts so it passes `typos` and mypy) and drops its 1,252-line benchmark harness; the helpers add 59 lines, the work-list tile scheduler. They do not import the `tokenspeed_mla` package at runtime.
- `core.py`: the planner and the compiled kernel.
- `decode.py`: the per-layer dispatch: the once-per-forward plan, the DCP arguments and the shape checks.
- `backend.py`: `KimiK3KvBalancedMLABackend`, `KimiK3KvBalancedMLAMetadataBuilder` and `KimiK3KvBalancedMLAImpl`. The impl's `forward_mqa` runs the kernel.
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py`: the `KIMI_K3_KV_BALANCED_MLA` entry.

Kimi-K3's MLA layer (`mla.py`) is unchanged: it calls the selected backend's `forward_mqa`.

**Why a standalone backend.** The backend is about 190 lines on the common MLA classes, and it states everything the kernel relies on itself, so a later change to `TOKENSPEED_MLA` can't silently change what this backend runs:
- the FP8 KV cache layout (576 values per token, pages of 32 or 64);
- the decode metadata (`seq_lens`, `block_table`, `dcp_tot_seq_lens`) with uniform query lengths and `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs;
- the packed FP8 query from the common MLA impl;
- the base-2 LSE convention of the DCP combine (`lse_base_on_e=False`);
- non-causal multi-token decode for the DSpark draft, with and without DCP.

Prefill uses the configured MLA prefill backend, as in the other MLA backends.

**Supported configurations.** An FP8 E4M3 KV cache, an SM10x GPU, a BF16 model and MLA dimensions (`qk_nope_head_dim`, `qk_rope_head_dim`, `v_head_dim`, `kv_lora_rank`) = (128, 64, 128, 512); backend selection rejects anything else with the reason. Alibi, sliding window, soft cap and non-decoder attention raise a `ValueError` when the layer is built. The kernel also needs more than 64 query rows per request (heads × query tokens) and at most as many requests as it plans for; the head count isn't known at selection, so these fail at model build with a `ValueError`. There is no fallback decode: a decode step the kernel can't run raises a `ValueError` with the reason. In the end-to-end runs every decode shape (target verify q=1–5, draft q=4) ran on the kernel. `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size` is read from the parallel config on every call, since NIXL P/D sets it after the model is built. The DSpark draft takes its backend from the speculative config's `attention_backend`.

**Tradeoffs and limitations:**
- **Size:** the vendored kernel adds about 4.9K lines. Integrating through the `tokenspeed_mla` package instead (reusing its compiled kernel with planned per-request splits) gave about 20% less speedup in our microbenchmarks. The work-list scheduler, direct output and P prescale need kernel changes.
- **Memory:** the split-KV scratch is sized as requests × query tiles × 8 splits of FP16 partial outputs. That's about 0.5 GB for 128 requests at heads=96, q=5, versus about 0.23 GB for TokenSpeed's SM-based bound; it's logged at startup.
- **Host syncs:** by inspection, the decode path adds none. Planning is a device kernel, and the once-per-forward check compares the forward context and a data pointer. This was not checked with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`.

commits.pr_title: [CI] List one test path per line in Buildkite pytest commands to avoid merge conflicts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Many Buildkite commands list several test files (or `--ignore` / `--deselect` paths) on one line, e.g. `models_basic.yaml` runs 13 files in a single 500-character `pytest` line. Two PRs that each add a test to the same job conflict on that line. This PR puts every test path on its own line, with no change to what CI runs.

## Claims

- Every pytest command that names 2 or more paths (counting `--ignore` / `--deselect`) now has one path per line: ~105 commands in `test_areas/`, `test-amd.yaml`, `intel_jobs/`, `hardware_tests/cpu.yaml`, `run-intel-ci-test.sh`, plus the L4 2-node command in `distributed.yaml`.
- No CI behavior change: all edited yaml loads to the same command strings as `main`.
- `check_test_tethering.py` now joins `\`-continued lines. Without this, the `|`-block edits here would make the tethering gate count every test as tethered.
- `tests/AGENTS.md` documents the convention.

## Validation

- **Same commands.** `yaml.safe_load` of each of the 25 edited `>-` yaml files equals `main`. The 2 `|`-block files (`cpu.yaml`, `models_distributed.yaml`) and `run-intel-ci-test.sh` equal `main` once `\`+newline is joined (what bash does). `bash -n` passes.
- **Same pipelines.** The ci-infra pipeline generator (`vllm-project/ci-infra` e28b4ff355) produces byte-identical step scripts for every `>-` file. `test-amd.yaml` rendered through `test-template-amd.j2` with `minijinja-cli` is byte-identical to `main` across 8 `mirror_hw` values x 3 modes. Intel yaml strings were also compared with PyYAML, libyaml, and go-yaml v3 (`yq`).
- **Same tethering.** `python tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py --all` prints the same output as on `main` (exit 0), and the normalized `load_selections()` list is identical.
- **Checker tests.** `pytest tests/tools/test_check_test_tethering.py`: 143 passed. 3 of the 5 new cases fail with `main`'s checker; the other 2 are a positive control and a guard for an escaped `\\` before a newline.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes.
- No `.buildkite` command still names 2 or more test paths on one line, except the line noted under Details.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the "same commands" check</summary>

```python
import re, subprocess, yaml

def norm(v):  # join shell `\` continuations, as bash does
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return re.sub(r" \\\n *", " ", v)
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return [norm(x) for x in v]
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return {k: norm(x) for k, x in v.items()}
    return v

base = subprocess.check_output(["git", "merge-base", "origin/main", "HEAD"], text=True).strip()
files = subprocess.check_output(
    ["git", "diff", "--name-only", base, "HEAD", "--", ".buildkite/"], text=True
).split()
for f in files:
    old = subprocess.check_output(["git", "show", f"{base}:{f}"], text=True)
    new = open(f).read()
    if f.endswith(".sh"):
        same = norm(new) == old
    else:
        same = norm(yaml.safe_load(new)) == norm(yaml.safe_load(old))
    print("OK  " if same else "DIFF", f)
```

</details>

## Details

**Format.** Single-line commands become `>-` folded blocks: `pytest -v -s` on the first line, then one path per line. Option groups (`-k '...'`, `-m x`, `--shard-id=.. --num-shards=..`) stay on one line, and argument order is unchanged. `>-` is already used in `engine.yaml`, `compile.yaml`, and the Intel jobs, and every line in it is literal text, so `#` or `: ` in a `-k` expression cannot break the yaml. Lines inside existing `>-` blocks are split in place. Lines inside `|` blocks use shell `\` continuations, as `cpu.yaml` already does.

Two rules when editing a `>-` block:
- Keep every line at the same indent. A more-indented line keeps its newline.
- Delete a path line instead of commenting it out. A `#` line turns the rest of the command into a shell comment.

**Tethering checker.** `_split_shell_stages` tokenizes with `shlex`, which keeps an escaped newline inside the token. Existing `cpu.yaml` blocks only worked because `normalize_test_path` strips the leading `\n`. An indented continuation, as in `models_distributed.yaml` here, yields a bare `"\n"` token. It normalizes to `""`, which matches every test, so the full scan reported all 26 allowlist entries as "now tethered". A continued `--ignore` (`"\n--ignore=..."`) was also read as a path. The fix joins odd runs of backslash + newline before tokenizing, the same as `_parse_shell_script` already does for scripts. It changes no selection parsed from `main`'s pipelines.

**Scope.**
- The rule is 2 or more paths, so it is easy to state and check. 39 of the rewritten commands are a directory plus one `--ignore`.
- The few existing hanging-indent lists in `kernels.yaml` / `test-amd.yaml` are already one path per line and are left as they are.
- Not changed: `intel_jobs/models_multimodal_intel.yaml:76` is missing a trailing `&&` (since #59865), so `pytest ... -m core_model pytest -v -s .../test_qwen2_vl.py` runs as a single call. That changes behavior, so it is fixed separately in #TBD.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Release checkpoint page cache between language generation …
commits.pr_body: ## Purpose `:amd: (MI300) Language Models (Extended Generation)` lost its pod (exit -7, "Perhaps the container was OOM-killed?") in 3 of its last 5 runs: [amd-ci#15340](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15340), [amd-ci#15350](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15350) and [amd-ci#15384](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15384). Each time, the pod was killed during `test_granite.py::test_models[5-64-bfloat16-ibm/PowerMoE-3b]`. The tests in `tests/models/language/generation` load many checkpoints in one pytest process, and their page cache is charged to the pod's memory cgroup. The job reads ~208 GiB of checkpoints against ~133 GiB of effective pod memory, so even passing runs drop below 1 GiB of available RAM. This PR adds an autouse fixture in this directory that frees the previous test's checkpoint page cache when the model changes, using the same mechanism #61415 added for LM Eval. It applies on ROCm only. Consecutive tests of the same model keep its cache, as do the HF and vLLM runners within one test. ## Test Plan MI300X (gfx942), in the `rocm/vllm-dev:ci_base` image. The run used 24 of the job's 76 tests (~89 GiB of checkpoints), evicted the page cache before each run, and sampled the container's cgroup memory every 2 s: ```bash cd tests pytest -v -s models/language/generation/test_common.py models/language/generation/test_granite.py \ -m '(not core_model) and (not hybrid_model)' \ -k 'Qwen3-8B or stablelm or starcoder2-3b or Apertus or Domyn or PowerLM or PowerMoE or granite-swash' ``` ## Test Result The log shows `Released X GiB of checkpoint page cache` lines as the model changes. | | main | this PR | |---|---:|---:| | Peak container memory | 102.4 GiB | 28.5 GiB | | Peak page cache | 93.4 GiB | 19.8 GiB | | Duration | 21:16 | 21:52 | AI-assisted tooling was used to analyze the CI logs and to run the validation. The results and the change were manually reviewed. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this test.

Not run locally (no torch environment here); ruff passes. The `Entrypoints Unit` steps will confirm.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][MoE] Size the DeepGEMM MegaMoE symmetric buffer for one sequence-parallel shard
commits.pr_body:
## Overview With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `--enable-expert-parallel`, TP > 1 and PP = 1, Kimi K3 runs its MoE layers sequence parallel: each rank feeds MegaMoE at most `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, tp_size)` tokens. The MegaMoE symmetric buffer is still sized for `max_num_batched_tokens` tokens per rank. This PR sizes it for the shard. ## Claims - Kimi K3, `-tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`: MegaMoE buffer per GPU **10.73 GiB → 2.50 GiB**. - MegaMoE outputs do not depend on the buffer size (bitwise equal in a one-off check). ## Validation **Buffer per GPU** (one buffer shared by all MoE layers), allocated on GB300 by the vendored DeepGEMM with the arguments `KimiMoE` passes: 896 experts, top-k 16, `routed_expert_hidden_size` 3584, intermediate 3072, `fp8xfp4`, `situ`, no fused shared experts. EP = TP, DP = 1; TP8 ran on two 4-GPU nodes. | TP = EP | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | main | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | 8 | 16384 | 10.73 GiB | 2.50 GiB | | 8 | 32768 | 21.29 GiB | 3.68 GiB | | 4 | 8192 | 3.74 GiB | 1.66 GiB | | 4 | 16384 | 6.52 GiB | 2.34 GiB | | 4 | 32768 | 12.80 GiB | 3.74 GiB | DeepGEMM rounds the per-rank token bound up to a multiple of 1920 before sizing (the TP8 shard of 2048 tokens is sized for 3840).
Repro ```python # torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 buf.py (TP8: 2 nodes x 4) import os, sys, torch, torch.distributed as dist from vllm.utils.deep_gemm import _import_deep_gemm dist.init_process_group("nccl") torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])) buf = _import_deep_gemm().get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe( dist.group.WORLD, 896, int(sys.argv[1]), 16, 3584, 3072, mma_type="fp8xfp4", activation="situ") if dist.get_rank() == 0: print(f"{buf.buffer.nbytes / 2**30:.2f} GiB") ```

Its expert ring assumes every EP rank sends its full `num_max_tokens_per_rank`, so routing imbalance fits. With sequence parallelism each rank's MoE input is its shard, at most `cdiv(max_num_batched_tokens, tp_size)` rows at any DP size. The DeepGEMM warmup already uses this bound, and `forward()` raises above it. - **Why outputs match:** DeepGEMM picks `BLOCK_M` from the token count, not from the buffer capacity. - **Scope:** `DeepGemmMegaMoEExperts` gets an optional `max_num_tokens` (default unchanged); only `KimiMoE` passes the shard bound. commits.pr_title: [CI] Add missing `&&` in the Multi-Modal Models (Standard) 3 command
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#59865 added the `test_qwen2_vl.py` line to `:intel: (BMG) Multi-Modal Models (Standard) 3` without a trailing `&&` on the line before it. The `>-` block therefore folds two pytest commands into one. This PR adds the `&&`.

## Claims

- `test_gemma_ragged_audio.py` and `test_qwen2_vl.py` run as two pytest commands again, as #59865 intended.
- The same 5 tests run as before. Only the process split and the `-m` value change.

## Validation

`DRY_RUN=1` of `run-intel-test.sh` on the step's parsed command:

```
# main
... && pytest -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_gemma_ragged_audio.py -m 'core_model pytest' -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_vl.py -m core_model
# this PR
... && pytest -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_gemma_ragged_audio.py -m core_model
    && pytest -v -s models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen2_vl.py -m core_model
```

In intel-ci build 15243 on `main`, the step passed with both files in one process (`collected 5 items`, `5 passed`). `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

Without the `&&`, pytest receives `... test_gemma_ragged_audio.py -m core_model pytest -v -s ... test_qwen2_vl.py -m core_model`. It works only by accident:
1. `run-intel-test.sh`'s `re_quote_pytest_markers` swallows the stray `pytest` into `-m 'core_model pytest'`.
2. The later `-m core_model` overrides that.

commits.pr_title: [Kimi-K3] Route the fp8 chunked-context K/V pack through FlashInfer where it has a fused kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #56881. FlashInfer now ships `concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8` (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5667, #6163, #6373): the same fused bf16 -> FP8 MLA context K/V pack that vLLM's private `fused_kimi_k3_mla_kv_concat_quant_fp8` does, byte-identical, behind one public library function so vLLM, SGLang and other FlashInfer consumers share it. Behind that API FlashInfer routes by head count: a hand-written kernel for 12 local heads (Kimi-K3's 96 heads over TP8) and generated Cake programs for every other head count.

This PR makes Kimi-K3's fp8 chunked-context pack call the FlashInfer API where it has a fused kernel, and keeps vLLM's kernel everywhere else.

## What changes

- `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`: `has_flashinfer_concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8()`, the usual cached feature probe.
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/fused_mla_key_concat_kv_cache.py`: `fused_mla_kv_pack_quant_fp8(kv_nope, k_pe, *, nope_dim)`. It calls FlashInfer when all of these hold: FlashInfer exposes the API, the inputs are bf16, `kv_nope` is contiguous (it is the `kv_b_proj` output), and the device is compute capability 10.x (where FlashInfer's fused backends are built). Otherwise it runs vLLM's `fused_mla_kv_concat_quant_fp8`: fp16 inputs, an fp8 `k_pe` gathered from a plain fp8 cache, pre-Blackwell GPUs, or a FlashInfer without the API.
- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py`: both chunked-context paths (the layer's own loop and the DCP hook from #56881) call it for the fp8-query case. The bf16-query path and everything else are unchanged.

No new environment variables. FlashInfer's own `FLASHINFER_SPECIALIZED_KERNEL_DISABLE=1` forces its composable path if anyone needs to A/B inside FlashInfer.

## Performance

Kernel-level on GB300 in the Kimi-K3 deployment container (cold L2, median of 100, the same head-by-token grid as #56881's tables), FlashInfer's API vs vLLM's `fused_kimi_k3_mla_kv_concat_quant_fp8`:

| local heads | chunk tokens | FlashInfer vs vLLM kernel |
|---|---|---|
| 12 (TP8) | 16 to 131072 | 1.11x to 1.29x faster (hand-written kernel) |
| 1 to 128, not 12 | 1536 to 131072 | 1.06x to 1.26x faster (Cake programs; flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6163 tables, B200 and B300) |

At 12 heads and the 66k-token serving chunk: 120 us -> 101 us. Byte-identical on every row (55 rows checked in the GB300 run, plus FlashInfer's own 65536-pattern cast test). End to end this is about 1 ms of a 93 ms engine step at 70 concurrent sessions, which is inside run-to-run noise on that route; the value is one shared kernel path rather than a per-framework copy.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_kimi_k3_mla_fused_epilogue.py
pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_mla_prefill_context.py
```

New in `test_kimi_k3_mla_fused_epilogue.py`:
- `test_context_kv_pack_routes_to_flashinfer_only_where_it_serves`: with a stubbed FlashInfer, bf16 inputs on a served device go to FlashInfer with the nope split and the same bytes as vLLM's kernel; an fp8 `k_pe` or an unserved device run vLLM's kernel without touching FlashInfer.
- `test_context_kv_pack_flashinfer_route_is_byte_exact`: with a real FlashInfer that has the API, on compute capability 10.x, the two implementations produce identical bytes for the real prefill-context layouts (strided `k_pe`, 3 / 12 / 24 heads, 1 / 257 / 2048 tokens). Skipped elsewhere.

## Test Result

H100 (vLLM 0.31.0 wheel with this PR's four files overlaid, torch 2.13 + CUDA 13.0): `test_kimi_k3_mla_fused_epilogue.py` + `test_mla_prefill_context.py`: 46 passed, 9 skipped (the real-FlashInfer rows; that FlashInfer predates the API and the GPU is SM90). `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

## Scope

- Until vLLM picks up a FlashInfer release that includes the API (it is on FlashInfer `main` as of 2026-10-12), the probe is false and this PR changes nothing at runtime. Once it does, Blackwell deployments switch to the FlashInfer kernels automatically.
- Hopper and earlier always keep vLLM's kernel, which is built for SM90+.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Replace torch.compile'd AV draft-budget selection with a Triton kernel
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Replace adaptive verification's `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` draft-budget selection with a single-launch Triton kernel, JIT'd once in `warmup_kernels`. This removes the mid-serving compile stalls and cuts the host cost of every budget-binding step about 6x.

Related: #62539 fixes the same stall by pre-compiling the Dynamo specializations at startup. This PR instead removes the compile, which also removes the launch overhead it never paid for (details below). Credit to #62539 for the root cause and for spotting the `max_num_reqs` duck-sizing specialization.

## Claims

- No budget-kernel compiles during serving: one Triton JIT at warmup (0.45 s warm cache, 1.0 s cold) instead of 4–5 Dynamo graphs compiled on the first trimmed steps (1.8–4.7 s per process).
- Host time per budget-binding step drops from 76–90 µs (compiled) to ~15 µs. GPU time drops from 85–100 µs to 22–30 µs at typical batch sizes.
- Qwen3-4B + DSpark, GSM8K, concurrency 16 (H200): adaptive verification goes from 4,783 to 6,803 output tok/s (median), on par with #62539 (6,756; within run-to-run noise). Accuracy unchanged.

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py` gives 24 passed on H200. The new GPU tests check the kernel against a torch global top-k reference: K ∈ {3, 8}, {1, 2, 300} requests (300 crosses a block boundary), budgets from 1 to total − 1. A ties test checks that exactly `draft_budget` drafts are admitted. They run in the existing `V1 Spec Decode` (H200 MIG) job. `pre-commit run` passes, including mypy.

**End to end, Qwen3-4B + `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_4b_block7`.** Setup: 7 speculative tokens, probabilistic drafts, GSM8K 1-shot, 128 prompts, concurrency 16, 1×H200. All arms use the same build at `d561af5df`, run in alternation. Compiles are counted the same way as #62539: `TORCH_LOGS=dynamo` `start tracing _assign_draft_token_budget` lines during generation.

| Arm | Runs | Output tok/s, median (range) | Compiles during generation | GSM8K accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fixed verification | 3 | 6,507 (6,117–6,837) | – | 0.81–0.82 |
| Adaptive, main | 3 | 4,783 (3,072–5,541) | 2–3 | 0.83–0.84 |
| Adaptive, #62539 | 3 | 6,756 (6,735–6,785) | 0 | 0.83–0.84 |
| Adaptive, this PR | 3 | 6,803 (6,594–6,864) | 0 | 0.83–0.84 |

The script is the one from #62539, without `attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN"`. A separate run of this PR with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` completed with no errors (6,910 tok/s, accuracy 0.836).

**End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + DSpark.** Setup: TP4 + EP, H200, random 8K-token prompts. The metric is the warmup bench's worst TTFT (16 requests, concurrency 4, issued right after startup):

| | main | this PR | no adaptive verification |
|---|---|---|---|
| K=3 | 2,424 ms | 866 ms | 824 ms |
| K=8 | 1,815 ms | 789 ms | – |

Steady-state TTFT, TPOT, KV capacity and CUDA-graph memory are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Kernel microbenchmark (H200, median µs per call, host / GPU)</summary>

Host time is wall time across the Python call with no sync. GPU time is CUDA events around the call. `idx_mapping` is int64, as in `prepare_inputs`.

| num_reqs | budget | eager | torch.compile | Triton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 | 93 / 102 | 79 / 88 | 15 / 22 |
| 16 | 20 | 98 / 106 | 88 / 97 | 15 / 23 |
| 64 | 64 | 91 / 99 | 84 / 93 | 15 / 23 |
| 256 | 300 | 91 / 100 | 84 / 93 | 15 / 24 |
| 1024 | 2000 | 90 / 104 | 85 / 99 | 15 / 37 |

(K=3. K=5 and K=8 are similar, except Triton GPU time at 1,024 requests rises to 49 µs and 67 µs.)

First-call cost of the compiled version: 3.0 s cold (1.4 s with a warm Inductor cache), plus 0.45–0.64 s (0.11–0.16 s warm) for each of the `num_reqs == 1` / `draft_budget == 1` specializations. The Triton kernel compiles once, and later shapes, including 1 request with budget 1, run in under 0.1 ms.

</details>

## Details

- **Root cause.** `warmup_kernels` runs with adaptive verification off, and cost profiling never trims, so the compiled budget function first ran on a live trimmed step. It then recompiled for each 0/1 specialization (and for `num_reqs == max_num_reqs`, per #62539).
- **Why not keep the compile.** The op is about six tiny kernels and is bound by host launch overhead. Compiled it saves only ~0–20 µs over eager, and it still costs ~80 µs of host time on every binding step. It runs eagerly in `prepare_inputs`, outside any CUDA graph, so that cost lands on the step's host critical path whenever the host is the bottleneck.
- **Kernel.** A single program does three passes:
  1. Survival prefix products, stored as float bits. Values are non-negative, so int order matches float order; ineligible slots store −1.
  2. A binary search on the bits for the `draft_budget`-th largest value.
  3. Per-request counts above the threshold, with ties handed out in request order.

  Survival is non-increasing along a request, so per-request counts fully describe the winners, as before. With distinct values the result is identical to the old top-k. On exact ties, top-k's choice was already unspecified.
- **Specialization.** `num_reqs` and `draft_budget` are `do_not_specialize`, so the one JIT in `warmup_budget_kernel()` covers every shape. The kernel needs a `max_num_reqs × K` int32 scratch buffer.
- **Tradeoffs.** The binary search takes 31 sequential passes over `num_reqs × K` slots, so GPU time grows with very large batches (67 µs at 1,024 requests and K=8). That's still below the old path, and negligible next to a step at that batch size. I couldn't test ROCm or XPU here, where adaptive verification is also used. The kernel uses only standard Triton ops (`bitcast`, `cumsum`, `debug_barrier`, a scalar `while`).

---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep legacy WNA16 MoE dispatch on Triton under batch invariance
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`should_moe_wna16_use_cuda` selects the CUDA WNA16 MoE kernel (`moe_wna16_gemm`) when there are at most six tokens per expert and the Triton `fused_moe_kernel_gptq_awq` otherwise. For the legacy `fused_experts` path with `use_int4_w4a16` under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` this means a request's experts are computed by the CUDA kernel when it is processed alone and by the Triton kernel when it is processed in a large enough batch, which defeats batch invariance. Two more things show up at the kernel level: the CUDA kernel is not deterministic run to run (same inputs, different output), and with the fixed batch-invariant config (`BLOCK_SIZE_K=32`) it rejects group sizes above 32 (`BLOCK_SIZE_K must divisible by group_size`). The Triton kernel with the fixed config gave bitwise identical rows for every batch size tried (M = 1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 300).

This PR makes `should_moe_wna16_use_cuda` return `False` in batch-invariant mode, so the Triton kernel with the fixed config is always used. Nothing changes when the flag is unset.

Note: the modular MoE path (`TritonWNA16Experts`, used by the compressed-tensors and GPTQ/AWQ MoE methods when serving) already calls the Triton kernel directly, so this only affects direct `fused_experts` users and the `get_default_config` path; it is a hardening of the public API rather than a serving fix.

## Test Plan

- Kernel-level check on an A10 (`main` at `d09ff7763`): a random int4 MoE (128 experts, top-8, N=768, K=2048) run through the `fused_moe` test helper (`tests/kernels/moe/utils.py`, which calls `fused_experts`) with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` for M = 1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 300; row 0 compared bitwise with the M=1 result, with the CUDA kernel allowed (current behaviour) and disabled (this PR), for group sizes 32 and 128. Script attached below.

## Test Result

Each group size is run twice by the script: first with the CUDA kernel allowed, which is what `main` does, then with it disabled, which is what this PR does. The `ERROR` line below is therefore `main` failing; the line after it is this PR passing.

```text
COMMAND: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 PYTHONPATH=/data00/vllm-eval-mla python /data00/runs/wna16_moe_bi/kernel_repro.py 32
COMMIT: d09ff77637 [Bugfix] Give each data-parallel engine its own global RNG streams (#5 (main, 0 modified files)
GPU: NVIDIA A10, 580.126.20
group_size 32
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT = True | should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8*topk...) = True
# main (CUDA kernel allowed):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=True: row0 vs M=1 -> M=1 repeated:DIFF(maxabs=0.00195), M=1:DIFF(maxabs=0.00238), M=2:DIFF(maxabs=0.00171), M=8:DIFF(maxabs=0.00171), M=32:DIFF(maxabs=0.00171), M=128:DIFF(maxabs=0.00217), M=300:DIFF(maxabs=0.00217)
# this PR (CUDA kernel disabled):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=False: row0 vs M=1 -> M=1 repeated:same, M=1:same, M=2:same, M=8:same, M=32:same, M=128:same, M=300:same

COMMAND: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 PYTHONPATH=/data00/vllm-eval-mla python /data00/runs/wna16_moe_bi/kernel_repro.py 128
COMMIT: d09ff77637 [Bugfix] Give each data-parallel engine its own global RNG streams (#5 (main, 0 modified files)
GPU: NVIDIA A10, 580.126.20
group_size 128
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT = True | should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8*topk...) = True
# main (CUDA kernel allowed):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=True: row0 vs M=1 -> ERROR RuntimeError: moe_wna16_gemm, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/moe/moe_wna16.cu:314, BLOCK_SIZE_K must divisible by group_size
# this PR (CUDA kernel disabled):
cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed=False: row0 vs M=1 -> M=1 repeated:same, M=1:same, M=2:same, M=8:same, M=32:same, M=128:same, M=300:same
```

<details><summary>kernel_repro.py</summary>

```python
"""Kernel-level batch-invariance check of the W4A16 Triton/CUDA MoE path.

Builds a random int4 (group 128, symmetric) MoE, runs fused_moe on a batch of
M rows and on row 0 alone, and compares row 0 bitwise. Runs with the CUDA
small-batch kernel allowed (main behaviour) and with it disabled (the fix).
"""
import os, sys
os.environ.setdefault("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")
import torch
import vllm.envs as envs
import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.fused_moe as fm
from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
from tests.kernels.moe.utils import fused_moe
from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.config import int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config
from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import quantize_weights
from vllm.scalar_type import scalar_types

torch.manual_seed(0)
dev = "cuda"
dtype = torch.bfloat16
e, n, k, topk = 128, 768, 2048, 8   # Qwen3-30B-A3B-like shapes
group_size = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 32
print("group_size", group_size)
print("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT =", envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT, "| should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8*topk...) =", fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda(8 * topk, group_size, e, 4))

w1 = torch.randn((e, 2 * n, k), device=dev, dtype=dtype) / 10
w2 = torch.randn((e, k, n), device=dev, dtype=dtype) / 10
w1_q = torch.empty((e, 2 * n, k // 2), device=dev, dtype=torch.uint8)
w2_q = torch.empty((e, k, n // 2), device=dev, dtype=torch.uint8)
w1_s = torch.empty((e, 2 * n, k // group_size), device=dev, dtype=dtype)
w2_s = torch.empty((e, k, n // group_size), device=dev, dtype=dtype)
for i in range(e):
    for w, wq, ws in ((w1, w1_q, w1_s), (w2, w2_q, w2_s)):
        _, qweight, scales, _ = quantize_weights(w[i].T, scalar_types.uint4b8, group_size, False, False)
        qweight = qweight.T.contiguous().to(torch.uint8)
        wq[i] = qweight[:, 1::2] * 16 + qweight[:, ::2]
        ws[i] = scales.T
qc = int4_w4a16_moe_quant_config(w1_scale=w1_s, w2_scale=w2_s, w1_zp=None, w2_zp=None, block_shape=[0, group_size])

def run(a, score):
    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()):
        return fused_moe(a, w1_q, w2_q, score, topk, renormalize=False, global_num_experts=e, quant_config=qc)

Ms = [1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 300]
a_all = torch.randn((max(Ms), k), device=dev, dtype=dtype) / 10
s_all = torch.randn((max(Ms), e), device=dev, dtype=dtype)
for allow_cuda in (True, False):
    orig = fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda
    if not allow_cuda:
        fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda = lambda *a_, **k_: False
    res = []
    try:
        ref = run(a_all[:1].clone(), s_all[:1].clone())[0]
        again = run(a_all[:1].clone(), s_all[:1].clone())[0]
        res.append(f"M=1 repeated:{'same' if torch.equal(again, ref) else 'DIFF(maxabs=%.3g)' % (again.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()}")
        for M in Ms:
            out = run(a_all[:M].clone(), s_all[:M].clone())[0]
            res.append(f"M={M}:{'same' if torch.equal(out, ref) else 'DIFF(maxabs=%.3g)' % (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()}")
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        res.append(f"ERROR {type(exc).__name__}: {str(exc).splitlines()[0][:160]}")
    print(f"cuda_small_batch_kernel_allowed={allow_cuda}: row0 vs M=1 ->", ", ".join(res))
    fm.should_moe_wna16_use_cuda = orig
```
</details>

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Anchor Jamba streamed tool arguments to what was sent
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Streaming tool calls with the `jamba` parser lose the start of the arguments when the delta that delivers the function name also carries a complete argument pair.

The name-sending delta updates `prev_tool_call_arr` with everything `partial_json_parser` could complete at that point — including argument keys that were never streamed. The next delta takes the `cur_arguments and prev_arguments` branch and diffs with `extract_intermediate_diff(cur, prev)`, which yields only the new tail (say `', "state": "TX'`). The `{"city": "Dallas` prefix never goes out, so the arguments the client accumulates are not valid JSON, and the end-of-stream rescue in `get_remaining_unstreamed_args()` cannot recover it because the streamed text is no longer a prefix of the expected JSON. Non-streaming requests return the full arguments.

Multi-token deltas of this shape are routine since incremental detokenization buffers output — it is how the single-delta regression fixed in #48852 came about. That fix covers arguments arriving complete in one delta *after* the name; arguments that begin inside the name delta itself were still broken.

Both argument-diff paths now anchor to `streamed_args_for_tool`, the approach `llama_tool_parser.py` already uses:

- the same-tool branch sends `cur_args_json` from the streamed length, with a full flush once the JSON completes, instead of diffing against the previous completion
- the flush when moving to the next tool slices the unsent arguments by streamed length instead of `str.replace`

## Not a duplicate

- #50461 stops tail truncation by reconciling the last diff once the JSON is complete. It does not cover this case: with the prefix lost, `cur_args_json.startswith(streamed + argument_diff)` fails and nothing is sent. I applied its patch on top of main and the new test fails the same way.
- #48709 adds `count=1` to the `str.replace()` scan on the tool-transition flush. This PR replaces that path with length-based slicing (keeping a guarded replace as fallback), which resolves the same corruption; its regression scenario passes with this change.
- #48295 / #48852 handle calls that arrive whole in a single delta, a different failure mode; that limitation (#48294) is unchanged here.

No open issue describes the name-delta prefix loss; happy to file one if it helps tracking.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_jamba_tool_parser.py -q
```

The new test feeds the triggering sequence (name and the first complete pair in one delta, completion in a later delta) and asserts the accumulated arguments parse back to the original dict. Before the fix it fails with `JSONDecodeError` on `', "state": "TX'`.

I also compared the patched and unpatched parser across ~2800 random splittings of single- and parallel-tool outputs (strings, numbers, booleans, null, nested objects, unicode): the patched version produces complete arguments everywhere the unpatched one did, plus ~1700 splittings the unpatched one mangles. The remaining failures are the pre-existing single-blob limitation tracked by #48294.

## Test Result

Run against the v0.28.0 wheel with this parser file applied (main and v0.28 differ in this file only by an import-path move):

```
before:  1 failed, 9 passed   # new test fails, JSONDecodeError
after:  10 passed
```

This change was written with AI assistance; I reviewed every line and ran the tests above myself.

commits.pr_title: [KVConnector][Mooncake] Coalesce descending block ids to reduce descriptor number for Mooncake TE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Implements phase 1 of [RFC #63006: Reduce descriptor and WR overhead to improve Mooncake KV transfer bandwidth](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006). Reallocated blocks can arrive in descending order, which Mooncake's ascending-only grouping leaves as individual descriptors. Coalescing these blocks reduces descriptor construction and downstream Transfer Engine (TE) request/WR overhead.

## Claims

- For Qwen3-235B-A22B + 16k prompt, the descending layout drops from **96,256 × 8 KiB descriptors to 94 × 8 MiB descriptors**, with the same 752 MiB payload per rank/request. With 64 KiB Mooncake TE slices, data WRs drop from 96,256 to 12,032.  Reduces **KV xfer time by 56.38%** (79.832 -> 34.820 ms) and increases **KV bandwidth by 125.32%** (9,590.51 -> 21,609.67 MiB/s).

- Reaches comparable performance with NIXL connector for 1-16k prompt length, as benchmarked in [RFC #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006), instead of a significant gap.

- This PR can **only cover jointly descending runs** (e.g. P `[3, 2, 1]` blocks and D `[10, 9, 8]` blocks). Anti-diagonal src-dst pairs (e.g. P `[3, 2, 1]` blocks and D `[8, 9, 10]` blocks) cannot be coalesced and remain per-block descriptors.

## Details

Add a `_normalize_paired_block_order()` helper in `_build_transfer_params()`, before logical-to-kernel expansion and `group_concurrent_contiguous()` (which produces `group_remote_block_ids`). For each request/KV group, reverse segments where both source and destination IDs decrease consecutively by one, applying the same permutation to both lists. This preserves every `(src, dst)` pair and lets `group_concurrent_contiguous()` produce fewer descriptors.

- Why normalize before kernel expansion, instead of inside the grouping helper: With two kernel blocks per logical block, source `[3, 2]` and destination `[13, 12]` expand into `[6, 7, 4, 5]` and `[26, 27, 24, 25]`. These kernel lists have no consecutive descending edges, so reversing descending runs inside grouping would miss the merge. Normalize logical IDs first to `[2, 3]` / `[12, 13]`, then expand to `[4, 5, 6, 7]` / `[24, 25, 26, 27]`

- Why not full sort: sort takes O(NlogN), we reverse segments in O(N) to minimize the overhead of the helper. We identify jointly descending consecutive segments, and each segment is reversed independently. With vectorized numpy implementation, the helper overhead is **0.2 ms avg**, **0.64 ms max** with 16k prompt runs.

## Validation

### Unit Tests

**138 passed, 2 deselected** across the Mooncake connector and hybrid-Mamba unit suites. The two bootstrap HTTP-client mock tests are excluded pending [#63122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63122). Pre-commit passed all applicable hooks.

<details>
<summary>Test commands</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --noconftest -p pytest_asyncio \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
  -k 'not test_register_worker_retries_on_read_timeout and not test_register_worker_raises_after_max_attempts'

.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
```

</details>

### Qwen3-235B-A22B E2E Results

Hardware, model, serving parameters, and workload follow [RFC #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006): Qwen3-235B-A22B BF16, 1P1D on two nodes, each with 8 × H20 GPUs and four RDMA HCAs (~48 GiBps RoCE each); TP8/PP1/DP1, block size 16, max model length 40,960. Each prompt length uses the same synthetic trace across variants: 150 requests at 0.5 requests/s over 300 seconds. Mooncake binary is main@74944a77 with `MC_RDMA_SIGNAL_INTERVAL=32 MC_MAX_WR=4096`

Values are means:

| Prompt | Connector | TTFT (ms) | TTFT delta vs. NIXL | KV BW (MiB/s) | KV BW delta vs. NIXL | Xfer time (ms) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1K | MC Before | 172.01 | +13.84% | 11225.49 | -24.82% | 4.272 |
| 1K | MC After | 168.36 | +11.42% | 21642.55 | +44.95% | 2.178 |
| 1K | NIXL | 151.11 | — | 14930.98 | — | 3.062 |
| 2K | MC Before | 225.72 | +13.78% | 10359.36 | -45.91% | 9.172 |
| 2K | MC After | 212.24 | +6.99% | 21678.17 | +13.19% | 4.346 |
| 2K | NIXL | 198.38 | — | 19151.58 | — | 4.704 |
| 4K | MC Before | 394.90 | +12.55% | 10198.04 | -50.29% | 18.674 |
| 4K | MC After | 365.38 | +4.13% | 21610.32 | +5.33% | 8.705 |
| 4K | NIXL | 350.88 | — | 20517.07 | — | 8.782 |
| 8K | MC Before | 770.57 | +13.28% | 9326.52 | -56.07% | 40.603 |
| 8K | MC After | 698.95 | +2.75% | 21986.85 | +3.57% | 17.117 |
| 8K | NIXL | 680.23 | — | 21229.52 | — | 16.965 |
| 16K | MC Before | 1695.34 | +11.85% | 9590.51 | -55.45% | 79.832 |
| 16K | MC After | 1543.78 | +1.85% | 21609.67 | +0.38% | 34.820 |
| 16K | NIXL | 1515.75 | — | 21527.40 | — | 33.518 |
| 32K | MC Before | 115834.41 | +8.69% | 6875.05 | -67.87% | 221.395 |
| 32K | MC After | 113426.24 | +6.43% | 10220.36 | -52.23% | 159.904 |
| 32K | NIXL | 106573.46 | — | 21394.52 | — | 67.050 |

After optimization, Mooncake's GQA performance shows:

- For 1-16k prompt: comparable or higher KV BW compared with NIXL. Each rank achieves ~21 GiBps KV BW, compared to ~24 GiBps (4 x ~48 GiBps HCAs) theoretical maximum.

- For 32k prompt: better than baseline before optimization, but still -52.23% slower than NIXL because of anti-diagonal src-dst block pairs. With APC on, MC After gives KV BW 21612.980 MiB/s and Xfer time 69.672 ms. See detailed explanation in the discussion below https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63142#issuecomment-6358485864.


### Execution Time Breakdown

We show the 16k prompt run execution time breakdown with the same approach in [RFC #63006](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006). Each call transfers 752 MiB, mean values:

| Configuration / input layout | Calls | Descriptors/call | Submit (ms) | Wait (ms) | First post offset (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before normalization, ascending| 600 | 94 | 2.275 | 40.825 | 2.881 |
| Before normalization, descending| 600 | 96,256 | 30.483 | 52.060 | 33.254 |
| After normalization| 1,200 | 94 | 2.464 | 31.382 | 3.247 |

- **submit** constructs and enqueues WRs
- **wait** polls completion while background workers continue posting and progressing RDMA.
- **first post offset** is the wall time from the C++ API entry to the return of the first worker WR post. Normalization reduces descriptors so that TE workers don't need to wait for a long WRs contruction period.

## Related

- [#63006 — Reduce descriptor and WR overhead to improve Mooncake KV transfer bandwidth](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/63006): this PR implements Phase 1.
- [#60523 — Improving MooncakeConnector](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60523): broader connector optimization roadmap.
- [#57952](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57952): packed-region coalescing; does not normalize descending block IDs.
- [#62478 — Vectorize transfer descriptor build](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62478): accelerates construction while preserving descriptor values/order, including descending boundaries.
- [#60605 — Optimize Mooncake contiguous block grouping](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60605): reduces grouping overhead while preserving the ascending-only grouping behavior.
- [#63122 — Mooncake tests: patch the httpx module the connector uses](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/63122): independent fix for the two existing bootstrap test failures.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DFlash: run the aux hidden state FC in the draft dtype
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A DFlash / DFlash2 drafter fails to start when the target model gives it FP32 aux hidden states (Muse Spark keeps its residual stream in FP32). The drafter's bf16 `fc` gets an FP32 input. This PR casts the input of `fc` to the FC's `params_dtype` in `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM.combine_hidden_states`.

## Claims

- Bug fix: Muse Spark Open with a DFlash2 draft (`"method": "dflash"`) now loads and serves. Before this change, the profile run failed with `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype`.
- No change for targets whose hidden states are already in the draft dtype: `Tensor.to()` returns the same tensor and adds no kernel.
- This PR makes no performance claims.

## Validation

**Unit test** (runs on CPU tensors): `test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype` in `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py` builds a bf16 `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM` on CPU through its constructor (with the file's `_mock_draft_configs` helper), gives `combine_hidden_states` FP32 aux hidden states, and checks that the result is bf16 and equal to `fc` applied to the bf16 input.

Before the fix (this PR's base 5f63ea4 + the new test):

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -k fp32_target -q
vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py:89: in default_unquantized_gemm
    return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, weight, bias)
E       RuntimeError: expected m1 and m2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != c10::BFloat16
FAILED tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py::test_dflash_fc_runs_fp32_target_hidden_states_in_draft_dtype
1 failed, 103 deselected
```

With the fix:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -k fp32_target -q
1 passed, 103 deselected

$ pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
    tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py -q
34 passed, 92 skipped        # the skipped tests require CUDA
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX, check-test-tethering).

**End to end** (8x MI355X, `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, `--dtype bfloat16`, TP8, speculative config `{"method": "dflash", "model": "<Muse-Spark-Open DFlash2 draft, bf16>", "num_speculative_tokens": 7, ...}`):

| Server | Result |
|---|---|
| Without the fix | Fails at startup in the profile run: `expected mat1 and mat2 to have the same dtype` in `combine_hidden_states` |
| With the fix | Loads (`DFlash2Speculator`) and serves requests |

The GPU runs used the same change on an earlier main (6ee316e). Between 6ee316e and this base, main changed `qwen3_dflash.py` only in the draft quantization-config mapping (#63001), not in `combine_hidden_states` or `fc`, and did not change `qwen3_dflash2.py`.

## Details

**Root cause.** Muse Spark keeps its residual stream in FP32, so the aux hidden states that it captures for the drafter are FP32. `DFlashQwen3Model.fc` is a `ReplicatedLinear` with `params_dtype = model_config.dtype` (bf16). `combine_hidden_states` called `fc` on the FP32 tensor directly, and the GEMM rejects the mixed dtypes. `DFlash2Qwen3ForCausalLM` inherits this method, so DFlash2 drafters fail the same way.

**Fix.** Cast the input to `self.model.fc.params_dtype` before `fc`. We use `params_dtype` and not `fc.weight.dtype`: `params_dtype` is the activation dtype that the FC's linear method expects, also when the FC is quantized (an FP8 or packed int weight has a different dtype or no `weight`). For an unquantized FC the two are equal.

**Muse Spark DSpark.** `MuseSparkDSparkForCausalLM` (subclass of `Qwen3DSparkForCausalLM` -> `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM`) has its own `combine_hidden_states` override that casts to `fc.weight.dtype` and then calls this method. Its draft checkpoint is bf16 and unquantized, so the second cast is a no-op. This PR does not change that file.

**Not a duplicate.** #40334 proposed the same one-line cast for an AWQ + `cpu_offload_gb` case. Its author closed it without a merge after pre-commit failures, and it did not cover the FP32-residual target case. Issue #42588 (ROCm, `float != c10::Half` at the same line) was closed after #42646, which changed the RMSNorm path and not `combine_hidden_states`. No open PR changes `combine_hidden_states` (searches: `dflash dtype`, `dflash fp32`, `dflash mat1 mat2`, `combine_hidden_states dtype`, `aux hidden states dtype draft`).

**Cost.** The cast is not a host-device sync and is safe in CUDA graphs. For a bf16 target it is a no-op. For an FP32 target it is one cast kernel on the `fc` input, which the FC needs anyway.

**CI.** `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py` runs in the "V1 Spec Decode" step (`pytest -m 'not slow_test' v1/spec_decode`; `source_file_dependencies` include `vllm/model_executor/` and `tests/v1/spec_decode`). The new test runs the model on CPU tensors. We cannot add a CI regression test through `LLM` with real weights: the only FP32-residual target that we know is the 816B Muse Spark model, which needs 8 GPUs. We did the end-to-end validation above outside CI.

## AI assistance

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5). The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests listed above.
